summary: Calmest day of the month: Nifty 50-60 point range, Bank Nifty 150. Infosys, TCS (+100 in two days) and Reliance held the index; midcaps fell. Notable microstructure: index futures traded at steep discounts to spot (Bank Nifty ~50-60 points). His expiry book: 10,600 PE / 10,800 CE; neutral Bank Nifty structure with wings bought and sold.
lessons: Futures discount/premium versus spot is a live gauge of carry demand and positioning stress.

summary: Quiet consolidation ahead of the Trump-Xi G20 dinner in Argentina - a true binary event. Expects no final trade outcome, only talk announcements. Private banks (Kotak, SBI) and Reliance held the tape; FII net sellers, DII heavy buyers. His book: downside butterfly plus upside call ratio, positions light ahead of events.
lessons: Before binary events, sell structure (butterfly/ratio) instead of naked direction and keep size light.

summary: Pre-results Infosys structure: short straddle at 650, converted to an iron fly with long 720CE/580PE wings, wings financed by selling double quantity of 750CE and 550PE. Payoff: max ~Rs.3.58 lakh (15%) at 650, protection zones 710/590.
lessons: Enter earnings trades the day before results and exit once the event resolves; hold further only with a stop-loss.
Finance protective wings by selling double quantity of farther strikes so the hedge costs nothing from pocket.
A naked short straddle is high risk; the same view becomes limited-risk when converted to an iron fly.

strategies.name: Infosys earnings iron fly with financed wings
strategies.construction: Sell 650CE + 650PE (5 lots); buy 720CE + 580PE; sell 2x 750CE (10 lots) and 2x 550PE to finance the wings
strategies.numbers: 650CE @31, 650PE @27.50, 720CE @7.35, 580PE @8.40, 750CE @4, 550PE @4.46; max profit ~Rs.3.58 lakh (~15%) if Infosys closes at 650; protection 710 up / 590 down
strategies.best_regime: Results eve with elevated implied volatility
strategies.adjustments: Exit after results or keep far wings with a stop-loss; watch volatility crush
strategies.risks: Beyond 750/550 the financing legs turn the risk unlimited again; overnight gap risk

quotes: This is the second strategy, iron fly - a limited risk strategy.
I do not want to pay from my pocket to buy the 720 call, so I sold double quantity of the 750 call.

summary: Post-mortem of the Infosys earnings structure: stock fell ~3% after results yet every leg netted a profit - total Rs.8.95/share (Rs.10,740 per lot). Walks through margin with hedging benefits (~Rs.7.24 lakh) and the scaling argument for large capital.
lessons: Hedged option combos earn margin benefits - selling both sides costs far less margin than the sum of separate legs.
Option selling is about safely handling large capital, not about flashy percentage returns.
Exit near legs once the event resolves; keep far wings only with a stop-loss.

strategies.name: Post-earnings leg-by-leg review of the hedged straddle
strategies.construction: 650CE/PE sold; 720CE/580PE long; 750CE/550PE sold 2x - each leg marked after the results
strategies.numbers: Total +8.95/share = Rs.10,740 per lot (lot 1200); margin ~Rs.7.24 lakh after benefits for the 5-lot structure; ~1.5% in a day; projected ~4% in two weeks
strategies.best_regime: Immediately after results, when volatility crush pays all sold legs
strategies.adjustments: Closed the 650/720 and 650/580 pairs; kept 750CE/550PE with a stop-loss
strategies.risks: Far wings are effectively naked beyond 750/550

quotes: Option selling is not about making huge profit - it is all about handling the huge sum of money.
Though you pay 197,000 while placing the order, the next day the premium receivable is credited back to your ledger.

summary: Shows how to compute FII positioning from NSE's participant-wise open-interest report: index futures 44% long / 56% short, stock futures ~70% long. Contrasts with ~85% index-short at Nifty 12,000 to argue downside was limited.
lessons: Compute FII long/short percentages from NSE participant-wise open-interest reports instead of relying on TV sound bites.
Extreme FII index-short positioning (~85%) historically marks bottoms; read index and stock futures together for the true picture.
quotes: When retail joins hands with the FIIs, the combination becomes more powerful - that is why retail tracks FII positioning.

summary: Historic week recap: WTI crude settled at -$37; Facebook invested ~45,000 crore in Jio (Reliance +10%); Gilead drug news lifted Monday to 9,384; PM stimulus meeting produced nothing; range 9,000-9,500 with resistance 9,300-9,400.
lessons: A single mega-news (Jio-Facebook) can lift the whole index via its heavyweight.
Known, expected events (PM stimulus) that don't materialize lead to consolidation, not crash.

summary: Contrasts results timing and IV: Infosys declares after hours (ATM IV ~67) while IndusInd declares intraday (ATM IV ~140). Plan: sell May-series 400CE+400PE straddle, hedge with current-month 500CE/300PE; net ~Rs.94.55/share (Rs.37,800/lot) on ~Rs.60,000 margin.
lessons: For high-IV stocks, sell the next-month straddle - richer premium with relatively smaller risk - and hedge with current-month wings.
Results timing matters: after-hours declarations carry gap risk, intraday declarations let you react.
ATM IV doubling between a quiet IT major and a volatile bank shows why event trades must be sized by IV, not by price.

strategies.name: IndusInd Bank earnings hedged straddle (May series)
strategies.construction: Sell May 400CE @62 + 400PE @52; buy current-month 500CE @4.25 + 300PE @5.25 as protection
strategies.numbers: Net premium ~Rs.94.55/share = Rs.37,800 per lot; margin ~Rs.60,000; >50% return if IndusInd closes near 400 at May expiry
strategies.best_regime: High-IV stock ahead of results; next-month premium rich relative to risk
strategies.adjustments: Exit opportunity after the results; avoid holding the full month
strategies.risks: Very large move beyond the wings; one month is a long time in trading

quotes: One month is a very long time in trading.
In IndusInd, the long strangle can be in the current month to reduce the cost.

summary: IndusInd Bank profit fell 77% but stock closed ~15-17% higher because market expected 95% fall - expectation vs absolute drives expiry-day moves. Precedent: Bank of Baroda +25% after worst-ever loss. Teaches adjustment philosophy and the bus/pothole analogy.
lessons: Prices move on results versus expectations, not on absolute results - better-than-feared can rally
On expiry day, stocks can move opposite to results as shorts cover
Never copy someone's strategy blindly unless you have their capital and skills (bus-pothole analogy)
Without extra capital and adjustment skills, your only tool is a stop-loss in your mind

strategies.name: IndusInd earnings-day iron-fly style combo
strategies.construction: Sell 400CE + sell 400PE, buy 500CE + buy 300PE (current month)
strategies.numbers: profit down 77% vs expected 95% fall; stock closed ~15-17% higher
strategies.best_regime: earnings day when heavy short positioning built up
strategies.adjustments: speaker's own adjustments not disclosed; states adjustments depend on additional capital
strategies.risks: big gap moves on expiry; adjustments need reserve capital

quotes: It is not the 50,000 or the 500 - it is what you get versus your expectation.
You cannot just follow somebody blindly unless you have the same capability of the person you are following.

summary: April series ended near highs (~9,850) but weekend brought lockdown extension and zero April auto sales; SGX indicated 500-650 point gap down (worst since March); monthly OI range 9,000-10,500; 10,000 major resistance (Fib 50%).
lessons: May is historically a weak month for equities ('Sell in May') - factor seasonality into OI positioning.
Known-bad data (zero auto sales) is priced in; markets react to surprises, not confirmations.

summary: Live pre-earnings trade: buy 1 lot 350CE (~2,440) and sell 2 lots 380CE (~1,190) - near-zero cost ratio. Max profit if ICICI closes 350-380 (month high 392, resistance 390-400), downside loss capped ~825, risk only above 410.
lessons: Structure pre-earnings trades around the stock's one-month high/low band
Buying 1 and selling 2 at a higher strike creates a near-zero-cost position with capped downside
Far-out risk (above 410) is acceptable only when the stock has shown no ability to get there

strategies.name: ICICI Bank call ratio (1x2) for earnings
strategies.construction: Buy 1 lot 350CE at ~2,440; sell 2 lots 380CE at ~1,190
strategies.numbers: near-zero net cost (~40-50 paise paid); max loss downside ~825; max profit zone 350-380; unlimited risk above 410; margin ~1.5 lakh net (2.53 lakh naked 380CE)
strategies.best_regime: mildly bullish stock pinned below known resistance into results
strategies.adjustments: not shown in this episode; speaker flags adjustment need if it gaps above 410
strategies.risks: gap above the sold strike doubles exposure; earnings gaps both ways

summary: Firefighting walkthrough on an ICICI Bank call-ratio position after a results miss: original 350/380 call spread risked ~Rs 0.50/share; by selling 400CE at 3.65 once the stock weakened, the position flipped to net credit and profit. Advises small traders to stick to indices.
lessons: When a thesis breaks, sell a further OTM option to convert the position into a net credit instead of accepting the planned loss.
Stock options move violently; small-capital traders should stick to indices.
Announce the risk of a trade before the event, then adjust mechanically after - not emotionally.

strategies.name: OTM credit-sale adjustment on a losing ratio
strategies.construction: Existing: long 350CE, short 2x 380CE (max loss ~0.50/share ~ Rs 800/lot). Adjustment: sell 1x 400CE at ~3.65
strategies.numbers: Pre-adjustment loss ~Rs 3,000; post-adjustment profit ~Rs 2,000 per lot
strategies.best_regime: After a results miss confirms the directional view is dead
strategies.adjustments: Collected credit exceeds the defined max loss; no further action needed unless stock reverses hard
strategies.risks: New short call adds upside risk; acceptable because view is now neutral-bearish

summary: Market reaction to the Atmanirbhar package: Nifty broke the key 9,000 support as FIIs sold over Rs 4,000 crore in two sessions; argues the package repackaged earlier announcements with under ~Rs 2 lakh crore true cash outlay and no tax/GST/corporate relief unlike the 2013 playbook; keeps only the market-facts, drops political commentary.
lessons: Announced headline stimulus and actual cash outlay can differ by an order of magnitude - trade the market's verdict, not the headline.
A break of a psychologically important round-number support after a disappointment signals continuation, not opportunity.

summary: Where-to-find tutorial: BSE results calendar, NSE company pages, and Moneycontrol's earnings page with expected announcement times (today/tomorrow only); explains IV-crush premium-selling around results; covers dividend/bonus/split calendars (Colgate 1600% dividend, GE Shipping, Sinclairs Hotel split) and aggregate earnings-season statistics.
lessons: Results timing is tradable information: premium sellers position minutes before announcements to capture the IV crush.
Expected result times are historical averages - only Infosys-class companies reliably hit them; build timing buffers into event trades.
Aggregate earnings statistics (share of companies beating, sales/profit growth) gauge whether a rally has fundamental breadth.
quotes: After results, implied volatility crashes - and the premium with it. That is the trade.

summary: US reality-check week: Nasdaq ATH despite 2M+ infections; Fed caution sent US -7% Thursday; Nifty closed ~10,000 Friday instead of feared crash (already -2% Thursday; Asia only -1-2%); IIP -55% (lockdown); consolidation 9,500-10,500.
lessons: Relative positioning logic: if you already fell 2% and Asia only falls 1-2% after a US -7% night, the gap-down gets bought.
Already-corrected markets have less downside from a global shock - fresh shorting invites short covering.

summary: India-China border clash hits mid-session: Bank Nifty gap-up 700 then -1200 then +600 whipsaw; Nifty -150 from highs. Speaker argues knee-jerk not war: no firing, stone-pelting clash; option premiums stayed calm - the market's own verdict; Reliance hit all-time high; buy-the-dip framing.
lessons: If option premiums do not rise on bad news, the market is pricing a knee-jerk, not a trend change.
A country already fighting a pandemic will not open a second front; separate sentiment shock from fundamental risk.
Geopolitical gap-downs in stocks on your radar are entries, not exits, when premiums stay calm.
quotes: Smart people will not have more than one enemy at a time.

summary: Corrects the Galwan toll to ~20 Indian dead with similar Chinese losses; explains unarmed de-escalation context; PM address line misread as retaliation promise caused a 150-point fall to ~9850; next day clarity plus short covering drove Bank Nifty +1000 from low and Nifty past 10,100; Reliance fresh ATH.
lessons: First-day casualty reports are often wrong; wait for official confirmation before repricing geopolitical risk.
Misread political statements create 150-point air pockets; clarity plus short covering reverses them within days.
Edge is reading the same news differently: de-escalation logistics versus retaliation narrative.

summary: Pre-results TCS structure: sold 2 lots of 2000 PE, bought 2 lots 2300 CE at 47.75, financed by selling 4 lots 2400 CE plus 1 lot 2500 CE. Margin 3.65 lakh, breakevens 1988-2508, ~82% probability of profit, max profit ~65,000. Thesis: TCS is low-beta; post-result IV crush pays the defined-risk combo.
lessons: Ahead of results, IV is elevated - defined-risk structures that are short premium profit from the post-result IV crush even if the move is small.
Finance a long call by ratio-selling farther calls plus a protective put sale: net premium near zero with a wide 1988-2508 profit zone.
Low-beta stocks (TCS) rarely make >10% post-result moves - size wings to the realistic move, not the dream move.

strategies.name: TCS earnings combo (put sale + call ratio with financed long call)
strategies.construction: Sell 2 lots 2000 PE; buy 2 lots 2300 CE @47.75; sell 4 lots 2400 CE; sell 1 lot 2500 CE
strategies.numbers: Margin 3,65,000; breakevens 1988-2508; probability of profit ~82%; max profit ~65,000; result after 5:30 pm, reaction next session
strategies.best_regime: Pre-earnings IV elevation on a low-beta large cap expected to move modestly
strategies.adjustments: Stop-loss or fire-fight if stock breaches wings; exit after IV crush realizes
strategies.risks: Gap beyond 2508 on exceptional results; assignment/liquidity on stock options

quotes: usually ahead of the results, implied volatility will be higher... when the implied volatility falls, we are likely to make some profit

summary: Live pre-results Infosys trade executed on-screen with basket orders: buy 800 PE, sell 770 PE (1 lot each), sell 2 lots 830 CE, buy 2 lots 900 CE. Max profit 43,000, max loss 1.6 lakh (only above 900 at expiry), ~71% probability, breakeven 833, net credit ~7,000. Context: Bank Nifty down 1,600 points in three sessions on HDFC Bank leadership-exit news; Infosys near its 850 all-time high.
lessons: Define maximum loss before the event: this structure capped loss at 1.6 lakh only in the extreme above-900 scenario, with no downside risk below 770.
Multi-leg entries via basket orders remove legging risk and execution hesitation - prepare strikes, quantities and side before the event day.
Along-the-way management matters: expiry-date max loss is not the practical loss; a stop can exit the structure for a fraction of worst case.

strategies.name: Infosys earnings iron structure (put debit spread + call ratio credit wings)
strategies.construction: Buy 800 PE (1 lot); sell 770 PE (1 lot); sell 830 CE (2 lots); buy 900 CE (2 lots)
strategies.numbers: Max profit 43,000; max loss 1,60,000 (only if stock closes above 900 at expiry); probability ~71%; breakeven 833; net credit ~7,000
strategies.best_regime: Pre-earnings on a momentum stock near highs where a moderate move is likelier than a blowout
strategies.adjustments: Stop-loss exit if stock runs through upper wing pre-event; roll after IV crush
strategies.risks: Strong beat-and-raise above 900 creates the defined max loss; low liquidity in stock options

quotes: there is no downside risk and upside risk is only above 833

summary: Live pre-results ITC structure: buy 2 lots 197.5CE at 6.55, sell 4 lots 205CE at 3.50, plus sell 2 lots 185PE at 1.05 as a willing-delivery floor; ~Rs 2.3-2.5L margin, ~Rs 50k max profit near 205, upper breakeven ~214; downside plan is taking delivery on a 5%+ dividend yield.
lessons: Pre-earnings ratio spreads monetize a range view: profit concentrates at the sold strike, risk only beyond the far breakeven.
Sell puts only at prices you are happy to take delivery - a 5%+ dividend yield makes the floor rational.
Broker margin tools can misreport exotic strikes; cross-check with a second calculator before sizing.
State risk and reward up front; never pass risk blame to others after following someone's trade.

strategies.name: ITC pre-earnings call ratio with put floor
strategies.construction: Buy 2 lots 197.5CE @6.55; sell 4 lots 205CE @3.50; sell 2 lots 185PE @1.05 (July 2020 expiry)
strategies.numbers: Max profit ~Rs 50,000 near 205; loss begins beyond 212.5 (upper breakeven ~214 after put leg); margin ~Rs 2.31-2.5 lakh (Opstra showed 41k - wrong); underlying 3-month high 208
strategies.best_regime: Mildly bullish stock in a range into results, with high dividend yield cushioning the downside
strategies.adjustments: Take delivery below 185 (long-term buy thesis); adjust/firefight on a breakout above 212.5
strategies.risks: Gap above the 3:2 short-call ratio (225+) after results; assignment/obligation on short leg

quotes: When the reward comes you do not pass it on to others; when the risk comes, do not pass the blame on others.

summary: Live pre-results SBI structure: buy 180CE at 16.70, sell 3x 210CE at 4.65 (1:3 call ratio), sell 160PE at 1.75; near-zero net credit, upper breakeven ~225, profit zone 180-210, willing delivery below 160; plus a Sun Pharma short straddle (520 +/- ~56).
lessons: 1:3 call ratios monetize a hard resistance ceiling: zero-cost structure with profit through the whole expected range.
Sell puts at levels where taking delivery of a quality stock is acceptable.
Fresh capital amplifies both rescue capacity and risk - reward never comes without increased risk.
Pre-results pharma read-through (Dr Reddy beat) can justify an index-style straddle on a peer.

strategies.numbers: Net credit ~0; profit zone 180-210; upper breakeven ~225; lower breakeven ~160; margin ~Rs 2.5-2.74 lakh
strategies.best_regime: Stock stuck in a 170-200 range into results; strong resistance overhead
strategies.adjustments: Take delivery below 160 (willing buyer); firefight/book if SBI breaks 225 after results
strategies.risks: Blowout above 225 triples the short-call exposure

strategies.construction: Sell 520PE @30.60 + sell CE @26 (at-the-money-ish, ~520 spot)
strategies.numbers: Breakevens ~464/546 (520 +/- 56); results day
strategies.best_regime: Post-sector read-through calm on results day
strategies.adjustments: Payoff posted to social; standard firefighting
strategies.risks: Gap move on results

summary: Full firefighting case: bearish Infosys put spread + call spread faced a 780->915 (+20%) two-day run after results; added/scaled put sales (780/830/900/850, doubled 900PE) plus 1000CE sale and ~Rs 15L extra margin; net +Rs 21,826 vs -1.5L+ potential; insurance-pool and capital-gate lessons.
lessons: Firefighting playbook: sell puts into an adverse spike at successively higher supports, scale quantity as levels hold, cap tail with far calls.
Firefighting demands deep additional capital (~Rs 15L on ~Rs 20L base) - never run it on a small account; his gate: ~Rs 1 cr for stock options.
Size so one failed trade costs a rounding error of period profits (insurance model), not a survival threat.
A 1%-per-month worst-case outcome plus collateral yield still compounds meaningfully - judge trades at portfolio level.

strategies.name: Infosys bearish iron-condor-style spread + firefighting ladder
strategies.construction: Initial: 800PE long / 770PE short; 830CE short / 900CE long. Firefight: sold 780PE, 830PE, 900PE (later doubled), 850PE, 1000CE
strategies.numbers: Potential loss ~Rs 1.6-1.7L; final +Rs 21,826; extra margin ~Rs 15L; Infosys 780->830->915 (+20% in 2 days)
strategies.best_regime: Adverse post-results spike in a stock you can sell puts on
strategies.adjustments: Ladder put sales at rising supports; double quantity only as levels hold; cap with far-OTM calls
strategies.risks: Continued vertical moves; margin exhaustion; doubling short puts is aggressive

quotes: You want to set up an insurance company, you sell in all the states, not only in one state - that is how option sellers work.

summary: Friday's 300-point Nifty / 800-point Bank Nifty intraday fall explained as profit booking ahead of the AGR hearing; Reliance dragged into AGR via RCom spectrum, expected to underperform; DIIs sold 16,000 crore over 1.5 months; range 11,000-11,500.
lessons: Severe intraday falls without news are often pre-event de-risking; judge close-to-close, not intraday.
DIIs book profits at highs and redeploy on 500-600 point dips - flow patterns inform dip-buying.

summary: Follow-up on the ITC call (bought ~198, now ~170, -15%): thesis unchanged - dividend yield above FD rates, effective cost cut below 170 by selling calls, patience and averaging down; high-dividend stocks are income plays, not momentum plays. New pick: BPCL - corrected from ~450-460 to ~350 on divestment delay; dividend yield ~4.65%; OMC earnings inversely track crude, and CME curves price crude flat (~$40-43) out to Dec 2022 and beyond. Entry paths: cash-secured puts (sold 350PE @14) or covered calls; full disclaimer.
lessons: Dividend-yield investing is a patience game: price declines raise the yield and attract institutions - the thesis strengthens as the price falls (if the dividend sustains).
Selling covered calls against a stock position lowers effective cost (bought ~198, effective <170) - income cushions drawdowns in non-momentum stocks.
Oil marketing companies profit inversely to crude: with CME curves flat near $40-43 out to 2022+, OMC earnings support is structural, not cyclical.
Event-delayed stocks (BPCL divestment) offer corrected entry points when the catalyst is deferred, not dead.

strategies.construction: Sold BPCL 350PE at ~14 (August 2020 expiry), cash reserved for assignment
strategies.numbers: Collect 14/share/month; effective entry 336 if assigned
strategies.best_regime: Stock corrected on event delay; willing to own at strike
strategies.adjustments: Roll or take delivery and switch to covered calls
strategies.risks: Assignment in extended divestment delay / crude spike

strategies.construction: Held ITC bought ~198; sold calls aggressively as price stalled
strategies.numbers: Effective cost below 170 after call income
strategies.best_regime: Range-bound high-dividend stock
strategies.adjustments: Continue rolling short calls; average down on dips
strategies.risks: Capped upside in a breakout; opportunity cost vs momentum stocks

quotes: The more the price goes down, the more the dividend yield - and more institutions will show interest.

summary: Third consolidation week in 10,900-11,500 after June-July's 1,700-point rally; Reliance below 2,100 on AGR dragging; power stocks (NTPC, REC, PFC) leading; expects eventual breakout, range 11,000-11,600.
lessons: Markets hammering a range repeatedly weaken it, like hammer blows on stone - breakout odds rise each test.
Mid/small caps rallying 5-10% while large caps consolidate signals underlying bullish breadth.

summary: Trump's COVID hospitalization is the global wildcard; Friday's Bank Nifty short-covering lifted markets near 11,450; interest-on-interest affidavit (government pays for loans up to 2 crore) already priced; FIIs flipped to buying; range 10,800-11,600 pending US president's health.
lessons: Verdicts pre-leaked via affidavits become non-events; watch what is already factored, not the calendar.
Presidential-health risk demands wide option ranges - sizing the band to the tail-risk, not the quiet tape.

summary: TCS buyback at an all-time high puzzles everyone; SEBI's 75% promoter cap caps it at ~10% of public holding, making the rumoured ₹3,000 tender worth only ~₹25-30 per 10 shares - yet sentiment added 7.5%. The trade: IV jumped 33→39 (IV percentile 64→82), so a 2700 short straddle (lot 300) made ~₹4,000 in one session on ~₹1.5L effective margin, targeting IV crush after results.
lessons: Buyback news pops are sentiment, not value: capped tender sizes make the arithmetic trivial - fade the euphoria, don't chase it.
IV percentile above 80 after a news pop is the classic short-straddle entry; the target is post-event IV crush, not direction.
Event-day option income needs margin math: premium received offsets posted margin (₹2.09L posted → ~₹1.5L effective).

strategies.name: News-pop short straddle
strategies.construction: Sell ATM call + put same strike (2700, lot 300) into an IV spike
strategies.numbers: IV 33→39, IV percentile 64→82; straddle +14 pts day one = ~₹4,000 on ~₹1.5L effective margin; target ₹8-10K by results IV crush
strategies.best_regime: Post-news elevated IV with binary event (results) next day
strategies.adjustments: Stop-loss on combined premium; exit into post-event IV collapse
strategies.risks: Gap through breakevens before crush; direction reversal

quotes: Don't go long or short on buyback news - sell the volatility the news created.

summary: Binary events explained (coin toss; Sholay joke). Nifty crossed 12,000 then fell 250 points (Bank Nifty -750) as Europe's COVID resurgence and the missed US stimulus deadline hit; 80% recovered intraday. October data: VIX rose in 8 of 14 sessions. FII +2,100cr (5,000cr in 3 days), DII -1,600cr. Reliance weak vs HDFC strength; double-top risk noted; 12,400 next if 12,000 breaks.
lessons: Binary events raise VIX and premiums in both directions - fear is not only downside fear.

summary: Week fell 400 points on European lockdowns and stalled stimulus; US election is the year's biggest event - contested outcome is the only bearish case; option premiums ultra-high (Bank Nifty ATM straddle ~2,000); advice: no directional trades until results; investors split 50/50 entries.
lessons: Markets want stability, not a party: any clear US winner lifts stocks; only a contested result sells them off.
Before binary events, keep traders out and let investors scale in 50/50 - insurance via position structure, not prediction.

summary: Post-election clarity unleashed FII buying (~5,000 crore/day, 25,000 crore in five sessions); Nifty 11,500 to 12,800 in two weeks (~1,300 points, unseen in 10 years barring bounce-backs); banking results strong; mocks 6,500/10,000 target-callers; Nifty PE >33; range 12,000-12,600.
lessons: Event clarity releases sidelined money - the rally after resolution often exceeds the pre-event drift.
Popular valuation rules (PE 28 = crash) fail in liquidity booms; theoretical rules lose to observed price action.

summary: November's FII inflow topped Rs 60,000 crore - highest-ever monthly; FII futures at 82% long flags month-end correction risk historically; support 12,800 / resistance ~13,200; RBI policy seen status-quo on high inflation; expects pause, not collapse.
lessons: Extreme crowd positioning (75%+ long) is itself the risk - the correction historically arrives by month-end.
After record inflows, 'most positives already priced' justifies pausing, not panicking; support maps from tested levels.

summary: RBI week ended with Nifty ~13,250-13,500; RBI's bar on HDFC Bank digital launches dented the heavyweight while PSU banks rallied on Ambani-insurance-sale hopes; cross-country check (Italy +26%, France +21%, Japan +15% in November) shows it was global liquidity, not MSCI; 12,800 = strong support; range 13,000-13,500.
lessons: When every country rallies together, attribute the move to the global tide (liquidity), not the local story.
VIX falling ahead of an event (premiums decaying into RBI) signals limited downside; fear priced out early is calm.

summary: December 2020: after a 3,000-point Nifty rally (Sept expiry ~10,800 to ~13,800) and ~50% Bank Nifty rally (~10,000 points), the speaker frames the 5 Jan 2021 Georgia US Senate runoffs as the global make-or-break event: divided vs unified government determines stimulus flow.
lessons: Divided US government stalls fiscal stimulus and keeps global markets uncertain; unified government (with VP tie-break) can unlock a fresh rally leg.
A single pending election can be the hinge on which an extended bull market's next leg swings.
quotes: The same way, in US, they have House and Senate... a lot of bills got delayed.

summary: Same-day second report: bought the 200-point dip, closed at day high, crossed 14,200. Recounted his 'technical analysis is bullshit' U-turn via horoscope-in-marriage analogy; longs in private banks (Axis +6%, IndusInd, RBL); IT stocks at ATHs; announced restructured cheap workshops/courses.
lessons: Give technical analysis the same weight you give horoscopes in marriage - a factor, never the whole decision.
One-day-before-big-event weakness tends to resolve strongly in the same direction after the event.

summary: Consolidation with huge Wednesday volatility: Nifty swung -200/+150 to close +1 pt; banks outperformed on sub-5% CPI; HDFC Bank overtook Reliance as India's most valuable stock. Infosys/Wipro beat estimates, Infosys ADR +3-4% pre-market. FII bought ₹1,879 cr, DII sold ₹2,370 cr.
lessons: Consolidation with volatility is healthy - it defuses future corrections.
FIIs buy in bursts after pausing to bait short sellers; watch F&O positioning, not just cash.

summary: Crude oil macro history: 2003-08 run from ~$10 to $150, US fracking self-sufficiency by 2017-18 breaking OPEC pricing power, crude at ~$50-55 after touching $26; bearish long-term crude view; ends with Kerala real-estate/Gulf-economy observation.
lessons: Fracking made the US the world's top producer and permanently weakened OPEC's production-cut pricing power.
With 5% margin, a 1% adverse move costs 20% of capital - commodity leverage, not commodity direction, is what destroys traders.
In a crash, a 100-rupee stock can go to 5; a 100-dollar commodity cannot go to 1 - commodities have a floor equities lack.
Prices of telecom and airfares fell/stayed flat for 30 years while everything else inflated - technology and competition deflate industries.
quotes: Crude oil need not come from $100 to $5 to lose the money, because they take only 5% margin money.

summary: Sell-on-rise shift: 14,660 flagged as the top for a week or two. US banks' good results still fell 5-8%, emboldening shorts; dollar index near 91 pressured EMs. India VIX >25 amid wild Bank Nifty swings. Key teaching: very-short-term sentiment follows FII F&O positioning, not cash flows.
lessons: Very-short-term sentiment is set by FII behavior in F&O, not by cash-market flows.
A strong pre-market plus against weak global cues predicts a big minus - and vice versa.

summary: Buffalo-and-flies parable: bull market shakes off weak longs then resumes. Four sessions 14,660→14,250→back to ATH 14,660. Netflix results lifted Nasdaq futures; IT and autos (Tata Motors, MRF, Bajaj Auto, Bosch) at ATHs. Post-result moves obey short-covering/long-unwinding, not fundamentals.
lessons: In the very short term, results move prices via positioning (short covering vs long unwinding) - fundamentals work only long-term.
Bull markets shake out weak longs violently and quickly - hold quality or stand aside.

summary: Contradicted TV rotation narrative: Bajaj twins +5% while HDFC twins fell 1% - results-day moves are positioning, not logic. At 2:30pm intense selling (Bank Nifty -900, Nifty -275) possibly triggered by the Serum Institute fire; recovered half by close. Told the slimming-shop parable against tiered advisory scams.
lessons: Never predict the day-after-results move - positioning, not the print, sets it.
Advisory upselling (silver/gold/platinum plans) mirrors the slimming-shop joke: the fee rises, the outcome does not.

summary: Corporate earnings are the core driver; monsoon/elections are only enabling factors. Reliance's commodity-to-telecom-to-retail re-rating (+400%) is largely done. Macro strong (GST, credit growth), but Bank Nifty's 1,800-point two-day fall was mere profit booking. Budget advice: close positions and watch unless you can adjust under fire.
lessons: Corporate results are the only core driver; monsoon, elections and policy are enabling factors.
Reliance re-rated from an 8-10 PE commodity stock toward telecom/retail multiples, and much of that re-rating is already priced after +400%.
Bull-market corrections are fast and furious - two days can erase weeks.
Best pre-event posture for the unskilled: be flat, watch, re-enter after; enter early only if you can adjust positions under pressure.

strategies.name: Budget-day posture rule
strategies.construction: close positions before Feb 1 unless skilled in adjustments
strategies.numbers: Bank Nifty fell 1,800 points in two days of profit booking; Nifty 14,660->14,250->14,780 swings
strategies.best_regime: before binary events
strategies.adjustments: skilled traders may hold and adjust
strategies.risks: event gap against the position

quotes: Kaikara maram daan kalladi podum - only fruit-bearing trees receive the stones. Only a bullish market gets profit-booked.

summary: Nifty crossed 14,660→~14,780 then sold off; Bank Nifty −6% (−1,800) in two days. Reliance −2.5% just before results (profit booking rule); Bajaj Auto +10% on results. FIIs flipped sellers Friday after a buying month. OI: 14,000 PE ~₹30, 15,000 CE max. Budget (Feb 1) event risk. Range 14,000–14,800.
lessons: Stocks that run up sharply just before results get profit-booked into the print; weak ones short-cover.
Budget reaction depends on positioning: pessimism ahead can mean a post-event rally; euphoria leaves no room for misses.

summary: Retail under two-sided selling: FII -₹1,700 cr, DII -₹3 cr; Nifty 14,500→13,950 in two days, Bank Nifty -3,000 in four. Tractor-rally violence, Fed night, and mega-cap results (Apple/Facebook/Tesla) ahead. 'Crying child gets the chocolate' - markets sulk before events to extract stimulus. Sold/cut 14,000 PEs into the fall.
lessons: Markets deliberately sulk before big events ('crying child gets the chocolate') - price in the sulk, not the panic.
When both institutions sell and retail must absorb, falls extend - watch who is left to buy.

summary: January post-mortem: Nifty 14,800→13,700 and Bank Nifty 32,900→29,700 (~10%) in days despite a dovish Fed - a falling knife. FII -₹3,700 cr vs DII +₹1,700 cr. Good results fell, bad results rose. Personal admission of January losses; budget plan: stay out, re-enter after; market enters budget de-risked.
lessons: Fast-and-furious corrections occur only in bull markets - they are evidence of trend, not its end.
Entering an event de-risked (1,000-point correction already done) converts event risk into opportunity.

summary: GameStop/AMC short squeeze: retail Reddit crowd (WallStreetBets, ~4.5M members) forced hedge funds like Melvin Capital (reportedly -$5B) to cover; hedge funds sold other holdings to raise cash, creating a margin cascade that hit global markets; CBOE VIX jumped 63% in a day; Nifty -1,000 and Bank Nifty -3,000 in days; stay flat into the Feb 1 budget.
lessons: Short selling means selling shares you must borrow and return (SLB in India; borrowing in the US).
Hedge funds cover losses by selling other holdings - one squeeze can cascade into a whole-market margin call.
Low-float, heavily shorted names are ammunition for coordinated crowds; price can go 15x in two weeks.
When big institutions are endangered, exchanges and officials move to protect them - 'too big to fail' shapes crisis response.
quotes: Retail people came to know that these big funds have huge short positions... so we will buy these shares.

summary: Full event-strategy masterclass: 10 years of budget data show close-to-close moves under 2% (only exception -3.26% was COVID, not budget); weekly ATM straddle priced ~3.3% move; long straddle/strangle usually loses. Better: put/call back spreads (max loss ~Rs 20k vs Rs 32k) and put/call ratio spreads or butterflies for defined risk.
lessons: Implied volatility is almost always higher than historical volatility - paying full straddle premium around events is structurally losing.
Across 10 budgets, Nifty never closed more than 2% from the prior close except the COVID-coinciding 2020 budget (-3.26%).

Even across seven major crises (Lehman, Greece, taper tantrum, China devaluation, demonetization+Trump, Brexit, Feb-2018 US flash crash), Nifty never gapped more than 400 points except Lehman and COVID; Bank Nifty max 1,200.
Back spreads cut max loss by a third versus long straddles and win big only on large moves in one direction.

strategies.name: Put back spread

strategies.risks: sideways market loses the debit; margin understated by platforms

quotes: The implied volatility is always higher than the historical volatility.

summary: GameStop week: Nifty ~14,500 Monday open to sub-13,600 Friday (−900 in 4 sessions) amid the US short squeeze; short sellers reportedly lost $20–43bn. Budget tomorrow — historically ≤2% moves, GST weakened its power. ICICI/Shree Cement weekend results. OI 13,000 PE / 14,000 CE. Range 13,000–14,000.
lessons: Don't fear the event everyone watches; fear the one nobody is positioned for (short squeeze vs budget).
In a firm bull market, 10–20% corrections are normal; up to 30% is within bull-market norms.

summary: Live budget-day trade log: sold 10x 14,700CE @ Rs 8, sold 10x 13,500PE @ ~Rs 137, bought 5x 13,800PE @ ~Rs 245 (plus a 12,500PE @ Rs 10 elsewhere) - breakeven 13,155, upside risk 14,720, max P/L ~Rs 12,000, 81% PoP. Explains far-OTM options moving opposite to the market in high volatility; silver 'next GameStop' squeeze attempt; markets rallying on short covering.
lessons: In violent markets, far-OTM options can move opposite to the index because traders buy them to cut margin - premium behavior beats price intuition.
After a global selloff, any good news triggers violent short covering - position for the squeeze, not the narrative.
Small-net-credit ratio structures can carry 81% probability with a few-thousand-rupee payoff - size for the risk, not the reward.
When everything hinges on one event, that event is the only variable worth tracking (budget, budget, budget).

quotes: In case a tiger chases us... all I have to do is run faster than you.

summary: 'Nirmala candle 2.0': post-budget Bank Nifty surged ~5,000 points in three days on ultra-low expectations - the FM was rewarded for what she did NOT tax. Global tailwinds (GameStop collapse freeing attention, stimulus hopes). Huge OI in 15,500 CE+PE straddle signaled the 15k push; 14,000 monthly support.
lessons: Event outcomes are judged against expectations - a market braced for the worst buys a neutral budget.
VIX rising during a rally is upside fear: sellers of calls are the ones sweating.

summary: Crossfire consolidation: SGX +60 sold off in minutes; FII +₹1,787 cr vs DII -₹2,076 cr kept Bank Nifty whipsawing (+500/-1,000) with no net move. Wednesday-volatility pattern held. Showed straddle theta math (15,200 and 36,000 straddles earning 90-300+ points/day) and the Aditya Puri sale lesson: value vs valuation.
lessons: Insider sales are valuation events, not value verdicts - employees give value, the market gives valuation.
When FII and DII fight with equal force, expect huge intraday swings and flat closes - straddles, not direction, pay.

summary: HNI playbook: park capital in Bharat Bond ETF (6.95% vs ~6% FD, indexation after 3 years, only 6% haircut vs 12-99% for stocks, PSU-bond safety), pledge it for trading margin, and never leave idle cash at the broker. Explains the 50% cash component is a broker-level rule to the exchange, so some brokers allow 100% collateral clients; deploy parked debt money into corrections.
lessons: Never keep idle cash at the broker - park it in yield-bearing collateral and pledge it.
Bharat Bond beats FDs after tax: ~6.95% pre-tax with indexation, vs ~3% post-tax on FDs for the 40%+ bracket.
The 50% cash-margin rule binds the broker's obligation to the exchange, not each client - some brokers pass it on, others don't.
Collateral haircuts matter: Bharat Bond 6% vs 10%+ for other ETFs and 12-99% for stocks.

strategies.adjustments: rotate debt into equities at correction lows
strategies.risks: interest-rate/credit risk on the bond; 50% cash rule at brokers who pass it to clients

quotes: We never bring money to the stock market; we only take money from the stock market.

summary: Global rate-scare profit booking: two perspectives on rising yields (2003–07 Sensex 7× despite rate hikes; crude $10→$150). Friday bottomed 14,900; last hour +100/+400 with no institutional support (FII +₹100 cr). 15,000 straddle ₹260–270; March OI heavy 14,000 PE. Bearish only below 14,700. Range 14,800–15,500-ish.
lessons: Rising rates have two readings — demand-driven inflation is good for profits; but yields also pull money from equities. Hold both views.
Mid/small caps and PSUs holding up while large caps sell = selling is positioning, not distribution.

summary: Recovery day: US $1.9T stimulus passed + J&J vaccine approval lifted Asia; gap-up held. Data checks: GST collections >Rs 1.1 lakh crore third straight month; India manufacturing PMI 57.5 vs China 50.7; India VIX crashed ~10%. Defines correction taxonomy (10% = normal pullback, 10-20% = correction, >20% = bear market) with 14,000-15,000 weekly range. Detours: opinion-poll tweet backlash and clubs/party joke.
lessons: Index falling >10% from peak is 'correction' territory; positioning and range maps beat headline fear.
Institutional flow tells (GST, PMI, rupee) separate sentiment dips from fundamental breaks.

summary: Rally punctured by US bond yields (1.41%→1.49%) and soft ADP jobs: Nifty -300 vs Dow -100. Broader market stayed green (A/D 1043:893) - calls it index management around F&O positioning. Sets up Friday's US jobs report and yield path as the swing factor; flags Nasdaq's stretched valuation as the global weak link.
lessons: Index weakness with positive breadth = positioning-driven, not fundamental - do not read macro into it.
Yield is the new headline risk factor: rising yields compress valuations of the most expensive assets first (Nasdaq).

summary: Expiry-week volatility (holiday shifted expiry to Wednesday): 200-up/200-down/200-up in Nifty; only private banks, financials, IT green. Surprise: FII +2,800cr AND DII +1,250cr - both buying. India VIX -9%. Thesis: five months of +50% showed first-half rallies and late-series chop; March sat exactly at 15,100 after 8 sessions; FIIs positioned light/short → upside squeeze risk; 14,000PE OI rising while price fell 100→35.
lessons: Light institutional positioning is upside fuel: crowded shorts get squeezed into expiry.
'I am a stupid guy - that is why I am an option seller': non-directional selling wins by not needing to be right.

summary: QE and taper mechanics: post-2008 and post-2020 Fed bond-buying injected liquidity that flowed into emerging markets; the 2013 taper announcement sent Nifty down ~20% (6,200 to ~5,100). Feb-2021's yield spike re-ignited those fears as the US economy recovered. Speculator etymology as vigilance lesson.
lessons: Tapering withdraws the exact liquidity that inflated emerging markets - the 2013 Nifty −20% template.
Rates rising from growth are benign; rates rising from withdrawal of support are the danger.
Long-term investors can ignore tantrums; traders must respect them.
A speculator is literally a watchman on the border - vigilance is the job description.
quotes: Indian traders watch US markets more than American traders do.

summary: Q&A: 'waiting for the big correction' guarantees never investing (Nifty 12,400→7,500→15,000 arc); Maruti's call premium fell despite the stock rising because event-IV crushed after auto-sales data; retail gains conviction only at tops; why crowdfunding trading losses is morally wrong; Reliance re-rating thesis; short covering vs long unwinding in one line.
lessons: Waiting for the big correction means never investing: enter when you have money, exit when you need it.
Event IV inflates option prices pre-data and crushes after - right direction can still lose to volatility value.
Retail conviction peaks at market tops and bottoms out at market lows - the crowd is a contrarian map.
Trading losses are the trader's responsibility; expecting crowdfunding is greed dressed as need.
quotes: People seek certainty in an uncertain market - and that is the one thing it will never give.
Market 7,500 to 10,000: dead-cat bounce. To 12,500: valuation crash coming. To 14,000: FOMO. Above 15,000: now it is real - conviction arrives only at the top.

summary: 'Storm' arrived: SC interest-on-interest ruling (borrowers waived, depositors paid - bank-negative on paper) yet Bank Nifty rallied as uncertainty lifted; HDFC Bank short-covered into top five performers. Reliance strong; RBI canceled a G-sec purchase (read-through positive for PSUs). Nifty ~14,900; March set to be the first red month after five up months (Feb expiry 15,100). Rajinikanth 'separate route' analogy for India vs global cues.
lessons: Markets cannot price uncertainty: even an adverse ruling rallies the affected sector once the ambiguity is gone.
On event days, positioning - not the event's face value - decides the first reaction.

summary: Most violent session in memory: Bank Nifty -1,000 → +1,200 → -700 (three-way ~1,000-pt swings); Nifty 14,261 → 14,993 → 14,274 with a 700-point 2:45-3:15pm collapse. FII -3,383cr (two-day -5,000cr) vs DII +2,200cr: 'long-term investors follow DIIs, momentum traders follow FIIs.' US weekly jobless at a 1-year low while rate narrative stays confused. April range call: 13,750-15,250; April = 5-week expiry + results season.
lessons: Three-way violent sessions mark institutional repositioning around expiry - reduce size, widen stops, respect gap risk.
FII direction for short-term momentum; DII direction for long-term accumulation.

summary: Local-vs-global tug-of-war: US at ATH while Maharashtra weighs a 15-day lockdown (second wave); Apr 5 Monday −400 on weekend restrictions. IT results week (TCS Mon, Infosys Wed holiday, Wipro/Mindtree; HDFC Bank Sat). Calls written > puts (15,000 CE wall). Both institutions sold Friday. Range 14,500–15,000.
lessons: When global and local forces conflict, the market whipsaws — trade the ranges, not the narratives.
Heavy call writing below price marks short-term bearish positioning even when the trend is up.

summary: Both FIIs (+437) and DIIs (+658) net buyers after two FII-buy days (979). Everything green except banks/NBFCs ahead of HDFC Bank results. India VIX fell but stayed ~20% above US VIX (SEBI option-price floor cited). December 15,000 straddle returned >10% in 10 sessions. Big 14,900 call unwinding = bullish tell (with humility caveat).
lessons: Call unwinding while puts hold = quietly bullish positioning.
It is difficult to predict the weather (days) but easier to predict the season (months).

summary: Third straight 'Monday mayhem' (Apr 12 −500+, cases >2 lakh, Maharashtra ~60–70k/day peak). OI turning bullish: 14,900 CE unwound (monthly); March precedent — 14,000 PE went to zero by expiry. FIIs back to buying; retail dominating like GameStop. HDFC Bank results slightly light. Truncated week (Ram Navami). Range 14,200–15,000.
lessons: Result-day reaction follows positioning, not the print — shorts into a bad number can fuel a +25% rip (BoB precedent).
One-third Bank Nifty weight: HDFC Bank's reaction moves both indices.

summary: 'Perfect storm' Monday: headline-driven selloff (record 2.75 lakh daily cases, remdesivir black market, HDFC Bank miss, bitcoin crash). Nifty low 14,213 (his 14,200 support held), then +160 recovery; Bank Nifty -1,500 intraday, +900 recovery. OI analysis failed - put writers squared up to hedge, cascading the fall. FII -1,633 cr, DII +2,355 cr.
lessons: In panic-hedging regimes, open-interest analysis breaks down - crowd positioning stops predicting.
When headlines drive the market, ignore global cues for a few days and trade the news cycle.

summary: Friday free-fall after Wednesday's euphoria: Nifty -400 from prior day high, Bank Nifty -1,500; FII dump 3,465 crore vs DII +1,419. HDFC Bank+HDFC alone contributed 120 of 263-point fall (both -4%, top losers). FII positioning read: 78% long index futures (sell zone 75-85%), 59% long stock futures. India VIX closed DOWN despite the fall = market treats it as aberration, not crash.
lessons: Extreme FII long-futures positioning (75-85%) is a sell signal; 45-55% long is a buy signal.
A VIX that refuses to rise on a big down-day says the market reads the fall as noise, not regime change.

summary: 150-point Monday gap-up; stable trade let India VIX fall 3% to ~20.22 - only the 2nd-3rd close below 20 in 2021. FII futures balanced 50/50. Metals index doubled in six months. ITM 15,000 put OI build flagged as bullish. 14,900 straddle ~180 implies 14,700-15,100.
lessons: Balanced FII positioning and falling VIX mark a stable regime that favours option sellers.
A rise in open interest on in-the-money puts is a rare bullish tell.

summary: Opened better than feared and recovered ~150 points; Bank Nifty +500-600 off lows; mid/small caps green while indices red. VIX closed below 20 for only the third 2021 session. Top five Nifty gainers were PSU banks. Both FIIs (-336cr) and DIIs sold ~1,000cr - 'who bought it?'
lessons: Option sellers must stay dynamic - roll the straddle to the new centre as the market drifts.
Be neither bull nor bear; be a chameleon - adapt positioning to the environment.

summary: Dow -400 on rate-hike jitters ahead of US CPI. Three global headwinds framework: Covid, rate hikes, US corporate tax hike. Recalls Feb-2018: a hot inflation print and Dow 'fell 10% in one day'. Midcap index at fresh ATH; expiry-day volatility plus US CPI in the last hour.
lessons: Higher inflation -> higher rates -> money moves from equity to debt: the chain that makes CPI a market event.
Expiry-day plus a macro release in the last hour is a recipe for violent two-sided moves.

summary: ~300-point high-to-low fall on US CPI fear; US April CPI printed 4.2%, highest in ~13 years. He closed all positions into the Friday holiday. India data was strong: CPI 4.29%, IIP +22.4%, GST 1.4 lakh crore - regime flipped to good local cues, bad global cues. Three-month range 14,200-15,400.
lessons: Go flat into a binary macro event when the tail risk is a 10%-type session - losing 5-10 points of edge is cheap insurance.
Rangebound markets reward monthly short straddles; trend traders starve, sellers eat.

summary: Against weak Asian cues (China PMI miss) India rallied one-way: top five Nifty gainers all banks (IndusInd +8%, SBI +5-6%), Bank index +4%. The FII-short squeeze thesis worked: 60% short positioning cushioned falls and fuelled the rip. VIX broke below 20 decisively (~19.6). Corona cases down to ~3 lakh/day.
lessons: When a majority (60%+) is short, falls are cushioned by profit-taking and rallies are amplified by stop-loss buying - the asymmetry behind the FII-positioning indicator.
Short-covering rallies can run against negative global cues; flows trump headlines.

summary: Second consolidation day: private banks (HDFC, Kotak, ICICI) dragged while SBI stayed green pre-results; PSU bank index +0.36%. China steel curbs knocked steel 5-6% after a doubling run. The last-90-minute slide was expiry positioning, not reversal - his 15,000 straddle closed profitable. US jobless claims lowest post-pandemic.
lessons: Late selloffs on expiry day reflect position squaring, not new information - don't read trend into them.
Expiry-day flow data is noisy; discount institutional numbers printed that day.

summary: Day of surprises: gap-up sustained to close 15,690; VIX -8.5% near 15; mystery 15,700PE (bought ~350) expired at ₹10 — 'boys vs men' conviction lesson; first expiry under new margin regime (0.33x broker extra-margin); IndusInd -7% on one-year-old Hinduja Cayman news, recovered above 1,000.
lessons: At all-time highs, stale rumors trigger violent sell-offs — keep hedges in place. Conviction means positioning on your view, not just predicting.

summary: RBI policy day (expected non-event, comments watched); tech→non-tech global rotation; Bank Nifty still ~2,000 points below Feb high while Nifty above it — PSU catch-up could drive 16k; FII long >85% five straight sessions; 16,000 highest call OI; US jobs data tonight.
lessons: Every dip is a buy while put-writing conviction holds — but always hedge positions at all-time highs. Highest-OI reads are muddied by margin-motivated combos.

summary: RBI non-event; US jobs 560k vs 650k expected lifted futures; full back-office reveal: ₹1.05cr cash, ₹2.14cr F&O profit in two months on ~₹10-15cr capital; Bank Nifty ladder (35,500-38,500 calls / 32,000-35,500 puts) +₹14.1L/week; long-term options +₹50L; 15,000 straddle from 19 Mar ≈20%/2.5 months; Buffett LEAPS lesson; simplicity message.
lessons: Simplicity beats complexity — plain straddles and ladders out-earn exotic math. Never sell short-dated options naked; Buffett sells only >1yr LEAPS.

summary: India VIX crashed below 15 (2021 low) with put premiums refusing to decay; Reliance futures pushed toward 15,800 swing high; PM 5pm address jitters (demonetization memory); IT outperformed despite minimum-tax worry; 15,700 put huge OI = near-term support; 5paisa franchisee onboarding backlog.
lessons: Event headlines spike VIX even when the content is benign — fear is always fear. VIX below 15 caps big moves.

summary: US CPI day: advised clients to cut risky positions and re-initiate after (asymmetric event risk); S&P 500 within 10-12 points of ATH; FII futures long back to 85%; expiry day — inside candle likely till afternoon; both FII/DII sold ₹1,100cr cash the prior day yet Nifty held.
lessons: Ahead of binary events cut risky positions; re-entry costs a fraction of gap risk. Expiry-day candles tend to be inside candles till the last half hour.

summary: Feb-2018 case study: CPI 2.2% headline → Dow -5% on day, -5% more after hours, ~-10% in days; his own ₹3 crore loss that day took 5-6 months to recover — asymmetric binary-event risk lesson; tiger-advice analogy for bearish calls that don't materialize; FII long 85%; re-initiation cheap.
lessons: Asymmetric binary events — risking 10% to make 0.5% — are never worth holding through. Exit costs a fraction of gap risk; two black swans can end an option seller.

summary: Nifty 14,200→15,800 (~1,600 pts) with India VIX 14.1, lowest 2021 close; FII futures long ~83% for 11 straight June sessions; Bank Nifty still ~2,500 below February ATH; heavy straddle/strangle OI at 15,700-16,000; range 15,600-16,000.
lessons: VIX below 15 means gradual markets, but eye-closed option selling into ultra-low VIX is the real danger.
FII long >80% is crowded positioning; the comfortable zone is 50±10%.

summary: Global flat ahead of FOMC (June 15-16); Adani/NSDL freeze-denial timeline dissected as possible short-seller play; FII index long cooled to 74%; cash-secured puts sold in Coal India, LIC HFC, PFC ahead of results to capture high IV.
lessons: Cash-secured put: sell puts 5-10% below price during corrections with genuine intent to take delivery.
Pre-results IV is elevated - selling puts in quality names just before results captures event premium.
When FIIs long% is 50-75 he is comfortable; above 80 upside is limited (profit-booking overhang).

summary: Both FII and DII sold ~800cr+ each ahead of FOMC (rare joint selling); Adani stocks fell again (Adani Port -7-8%); LIC HFC results disappointed, HDFC collateral damage; heavy call writing 15,800-15,900; copper fell on China reserve release.
lessons: Joint FII+DII selling before a binary event signals genuine de-risking, not rotation.
Post-event gap-ups would trap the heavy call writers - their covering becomes upside fuel.
Watch what China does with commodity reserves - it moves Indian metal stocks directly.

summary: Fed turned hawkish (two hikes projected by 2023); US and Asia fell, SGX -100+; FII+DII sold 850cr each; ITM call writing at 15,750; advice to ignore next-day price action after binary events; Infosys call-selling and call-ratio plans.
lessons: Ignore day-1 price action after binary events - positioning unwinds first, truth shows up on day 2-3.
Consensus is dangerous: when everyone is positioned one way, surprise news hits hardest.
Rates rising because the economy is strong is not bearish - 2003-07 was a great bull run with rising rates.

summary: Gamma explained as the rate of change of delta: on violent news (corporate-tax-cut rally, COVID crash, surgical strike), an ATM option moves more than delta alone predicts; the extra kick grows explosively near expiry, which is why sellers close before expiry.
lessons: Delta is the speed, gamma the acceleration — violent news makes ATM options outrun 0.5 delta.
Gamma damage compounds near expiry: a 50-rupee ATM premium can double on a 100-point move.
Option sellers avoid holding naked positions into expiry precisely because of gamma.
Gamma rewards the buyer who is right on direction during violent moves.

strategies.name: Gamma awareness for expiry-week selling
strategies.construction: Short ATM options held into expiry vs square-off rule
strategies.numbers: ATM premium 50 → ~110 (more than doubled) on a 100-point sudden move; normal delta move would be 50→60
strategies.best_regime: Never for sellers in the final days unless hedged
strategies.adjustments: Close/roll before expiry week; keep far-OTM hedges as real hedges, not margin dummies
strategies.risks: Whipsaw doubles short-premium exposure in hours

quotes: Speed is rate of change of distance; acceleration is rate of change of speed — delta is speed, gamma is acceleration.

summary: Vega/VIX explained: expected one-month movement priced into premiums; April 2020 (India VIX ~60) carried ~8% ATM monthly premiums vs ~2% in June 2021 (VIX ~14); binary events inflate both call and put premiums; VIX highs/lows are relative, not absolute triggers.
lessons: Premium is expected movement: VIX ~60 priced ~8% monthly ATM premium; VIX ~14 prices ~2%.
Binary events (elections) inflate calls and puts simultaneously — both sides pay for the coin flip.
Sellers harvest rich premium in high VIX; buyers get cheap options in low VIX — but low/high are relative.
A call can lose while the market rises when VIX collapses — delta gains get eaten by vega losses.

strategies.name: VIX-regime stance
strategies.construction: Sell premiums when VIX historically high; buy when historically low; never on absolute numbers alone
strategies.numbers: India VIX 60 (Apr 2020) vs 14 (Jun 2021); ATM straddle ~16% of spot vs <4%
strategies.best_regime: Regime-aware positioning around event cycles
strategies.adjustments: Reassess after each event; premium collapse post-event rewards pre-event sellers
strategies.risks: VIX can go lower/higher than assumed — relative, not absolute, thresholds

quotes: In April 2020 both call and put carried ~8% premium each — the market paid for any move, up or down.

summary: Axis Bank's weekend results supported Bank Nifty; an MCA report hit housing finance companies (-10% intraday, recovered). SBI's good results after 3pm lifted banks. FII net buyers, DII sold >500cr. US midterm elections the next day kept markets jittery; range-bound consolidation expected.

Powell's dovish remarks sent Dow +600; gap-up, short covering into 10,880. November's 5-week series ran 10,030 to 10,880 (~9%); HUL, L&T, HDFC, HDFC Bank +10-20%. 'Markets climb the wall of worries' - buy uncertainty, sell clarity. Bank Nifty 24,400 to 27,000. December risks: OPEC, US-China, state elections; positions kept light.
lessons: Buy when uncertainty is high and prices cheap; sell when everything is clear and prices high.

summary: First Q&A: stop-loss doctrine (slow poison vs quick poison), square-off vs counter-strategy depends on extra capital and skill, discount vs full-service brokers, basket/simultaneous orders, the 50% cash-equivalent rule applied at broker level, Bharat Bond/Liquid BeES as cash equivalents, hedging without adjustments is risky.
lessons: Stop-loss is non-negotiable: hit it and you can recover; blow up and you cannot (slow poison vs quick poison)
Square-off vs counter-strategy is decided by two questions: do you have additional capital and additional skill?
The 50% cash-equivalent requirement applies at broker level; brokers may pass it to clients (Zerodha does)
Cash equivalents: FD, Liquid BeES, liquid funds; Bharat Bond (~5% haircut) may qualify with some brokers
quotes: If you put a stop loss, it is like slow poison. If you don't put a stop loss, it is like quick poison.
If you lose part of the capital, you can hope to recover. But if you lose all the capital, you can never recover.

summary: Walks through SEBI's new margining on real examples: naked ATM options now ~1.0-1.3 lakh (up from 80-90k), but hedged spreads collapse to ~25-35k, cross-margined straddles to ~1.05 lakh, straddle-with-wings to ~45-55k, and an ITM put calendar under 30k - pushing traders toward hedged, index, defined-risk structures.
lessons: Under the new framework the margin system itself pays you to hedge: protection 200-300 points away cuts margin ~70%.
Cross-margining makes a short straddle cost little more than its single costlier leg - portfolio margin logic arrives in India.
Margin relief can seduce into over-sizing: four lots at 300-point risk recreates 1,200 points of exposure. Options trading is risk and position management, not strike selection.
Index exposure carries structurally lower margins (2% vs 3.5% exposure) - another argument to avoid stock options.

strategies.name: Hedged short option (spread)
strategies.construction: Sell 10,000C / buy 10,200C (200pt); variants 300-400pt
strategies.numbers: ~25,000-32,000 margin vs 80-90k naked; max risk = spread width
strategies.best_regime: any directional credit view
strategies.adjustments: roll wings as market trends
strategies.risks: max loss = width x lot; premium give-up

strategies.name: Short straddle with far wings
strategies.construction: Sell 9,500CE+9,500PE (July), buy 8,500PE+10,500CE (June weekly/next series)
strategies.numbers: margin ~45,000-55,000 after ~40-60k premium receivable; straddle premium >1,000 pts in July 2020
strategies.best_regime: high-IV months with distant wings affordable
strategies.adjustments: re-buy expired wings weekly
strategies.risks: gap through wings; weekly-wing rollover friction

strategies.name: ITM put calendar
strategies.construction: Sell 10,000PE current month, buy 10,000PE next month
strategies.numbers: margin <30,000
strategies.best_regime: neutral-to-mildly-bearish
strategies.adjustments: roll short leg at expiry
strategies.risks: fast rallies inflate long-leg decay loss

quotes: Options trading is not about which strike you sell - it is about risk management, margin management and position sizing.

summary: Bullish call vindicated: Nifty 9,000->10,200 in ~7 sessions as FIIs turned daily buyers; US May payrolls +2.5M vs -8M expected sent Nasdaq to ATH; recounts Nov-2018 elections->Balakot FII cycle; NSE option-price glitch Thursday hurt traders.
lessons: Don't be a bull or a bear - be a chameleon; markets change trend when everyone leans one way.
Always trade with the trend; fighting it with leverage (F&O) makes losses heavy.

summary: Q&A session: hedging as non-negotiable doctrine, SEBI lot-size revision mechanics, collateral/pledging differences across brokers, expiry-day-only intraday selling, pre-market mechanics, and repeated refusals to comment on unhedged directional follower positions.
lessons: Always pair an option sale with an option purchase: margin drops sharply and black-swan loss is capped.
Lot sizes are revised to keep contract value inside the SEBI band of 5-10 lakh, reviewed every six months.
Intraday option selling only on expiry day, when far out-of-the-money options decay to zero.
If you cannot explain what happens to premium when you exit, you are not ready to trade options.

strategies.name: Hedged short put
strategies.construction: Sell near put + buy a further-OTM put same expiry
strategies.numbers: Speaker example: sold 9400-put style positions; hedge put cuts margin drastically and caps loss
strategies.best_regime: Any short-put view; mandatory insurance
strategies.adjustments: Not advised live; know risk-reward before entry
strategies.risks: Unhedged version: margin cascade and uncapped gap risk

quotes: If you want to be successful in stock market, you need to have hedge.

summary: Historic no-news rally: 10,800 to ~11,950 (1,150 points in 10 sessions) on RBI dovishness and FII buying; compares to 2009's election-day circuit; results week ahead (IT heavy); warns of correction when all looks good; range 11,500-12,200.
lessons: 'Markets can stay irrational longer than you can stay bankrupt' - ride trends with trailing stops rather than shorting strength.
Corrections tend to arrive when everything looks best; caution on longs, but never fight an uptrend by shorting it.

summary: Nifty took out its all-time high (~12,427) on Biden's election clarity, FII inflows of 10,000cr in two sessions, MSCI rebalancing (~18,000cr) and Pfizer-BioNTech's >90% vaccine efficacy. Lead-vs-lag indicator doctrine; retail 85% short, FII 75% short in F&O yet cash buyers; HDFC Bank FII-limit arbitrage story; bus-pothole lesson on copying big players; Bank Nifty still ~4,000-5,000 below its ATH.
lessons: Markets price the lead indicator six months ahead, not today's lagging data.

summary: Detailed fundamental case for Sun TV: 65-70% operating margins (claimed India's highest among listed peers), PE 12-15 vs Zee's 40-45, >5% dividend yield, RoCE ~30%; valuation discount attributed to political-overhang (Aircel-Maxis case); May 2021 Tamil Nadu election as potential re-rating catalyst.
lessons: A durable, dominant media franchise can trade at a fraction of peer multiples when saddled with a legal/political overhang - the discount itself is the opportunity if the overhang clears.
Covered-call writing against a long holding lowers cost basis (speaker's own method for this stock).
RoCE and RoE both above 20% plus dividend yield above FD rates is his screen for quality mid-caps.

strategies.name: Covered call on a long-term holding (mentioned method)
strategies.construction: Buy shares (in lot-size multiples), sell ATM/slightly OTM calls each cycle
strategies.numbers: not specified beyond 'reduce my cost price'
strategies.best_regime: sideways-to-mildly-bullish phases for a stock you want to own long term
strategies.adjustments: roll calls as stock moves
strategies.risks: upside capped; stock can enter F&O ban period, making hedging harder (noted for this stock)

quotes: Once upon a time, TV and Sun TV, they are synonymous words.

summary: MSCI deleted three Chinese telecom stocks Friday → Nifty +200 to ~14,350; FIIs bought >₹6,000 cr vs ~₹1,500 cr expected. Democrats sweep Georgia; Biden inauguration Jan 20; FM's '100-year budget' comment. Nifty-PE-28 correction myth challenged. IT results week ahead. Range 14,000–14,800, bullish.
lessons: A market that ignores a historically bearish valuation trigger (PE 28) is telling you this cycle is different — position with it, not against it.
Results-season trading rule: stocks that ran up before results get sold on good numbers; beaten-down ones short-cover.

summary: Mission Options E09: classifies strikes as ITM/ATM/OTM relative to spot with NSE chain color-coding (white = OTM, yellow = ITM for calls); compares cost, probability and payoff of 12,500CE (600), 13,000CE (275) and 13,500CE (75) with expiry scenarios at 13,400/13,000/12,500; concludes ITM is his preferred choice for higher win probability.
lessons: ITM options cost more but have the highest win probability; OTM options are cheap but rarely win - retail's lottery-ticket bias is buying far OTM.
ATM sits between: moderate premium, moderate probability.
Strike selection is a probability-reward trade-off: same view, three very different payoff distributions (worked scenarios at 13,400/13,000/12,500).
NSE chain color-codes calls: white = OTM, yellow = ITM (reversed for puts).

strategies.name: Strike-selection framework (ITM vs ATM vs OTM)
strategies.construction: Same directional view expressed via 12,500CE / 13,000CE / 13,500CE with spot ~13,000
strategies.best_regime: ITM for high-probability moderate moves; OTM only for large fast moves
strategies.adjustments: exit anytime; premium decays
strategies.risks: OTM total loss most probable; ITM larger absolute rupee loss

quotes: In the money options are high risk and high reward and out of the money options are low risk and low reward.

summary: Unexplained two-day Bank Nifty fall (-6%) resolved as news of a Sikkim border clash - price moved before headlines. Nifty fell 250 points in minutes; Reliance alone drove 80 of 130 points down post-results. Lesson: markets know first, and bad news gets pre-priced (IT's odd weakness despite currency logic).
lessons: Markets know everything before you do - unexplained persistent selling is itself information.
News confirmed later was already traded earlier: insiders or fast actors front-run headlines.
Bad news can be pre-priced: check sector behavior that contradicts the obvious reaction (IT fell despite a weaker-rupee benefit) to see if damage is done.
Never predict direction immediately after results - let the position, not the narrative, settle.
quotes: There is something called the market efficiency hypothesis... you will be the last person to know if something important happens.

summary: Budget-rally week: Bank Nifty +6,000+, Nifty +1,400; SBI 275→400 in ~6 sessions on results; FIIs re-flipped buyers. US stimulus: 50–50 Senate, VP Harris tie-break passed budget resolution (Feb 5); best US week since November. ~20% of Nifty50 results due. Support 14,500, resistance 15,500.
lessons: A stable government is the most important precondition for a sustained bull market — policy-gridlock resolution is bullish regardless of party.
Good results move stocks violently; index impact follows later — trade the stocks, not the index, in results season.

summary: Post-budget consolidation: Nifty pinned 15,000–15,250 (~250-pt range), Bank Nifty 35,500–36,600 with 700–800-point intraday swings; Friday afternoon Nifty −160 while Bank Nifty held; ICICI ATH +2.5%. CPI/IIP good. 14,000 PE ₹50→₹16. Strategy: sell puts on every 100-pt dip. Range 14,800–15,500.
lessons: The man-and-dog analogy: the economy is the man, the market the dog — the dog wanders but must travel with the man.
During consolidations, aggressive near-strike call writers become squeeze fuel for the next up-move.

summary: Bank Nifty 'dream rally': +1,400 points vs Nifty +130-140; 30,000 (budget day) to 37,500 in ten sessions (+25%). Argues DIIs sell on mutual-fund redemption pressure from nervous retail; advises holding and hedging rather than exiting. Petrol-vs-Virat-Kohli-100 joke and 'PR Sundar indicator' joke (self-referential, drop).
lessons: Retail redemption pressure, not DII conviction, drives DII selling in melt-ups; exit via hedges, not selling long-term holdings.
Equity pays years of returns in a few weeks; missing those weeks is the real long-term risk.

summary: Vindication of an Aug-2020 'gold peaked' call: gold below $1,700 vs Bank of America's $3,000/18-month forecast. Gold's Indian price = international price × USDINR × import duty. 2013-21 jewellery gold (~₹3,000 to ~₹4,500/g) underperformed bank FDs; duty cut 12.5% to 10% in Budget 2021.
lessons: Indian gold price decomposes into international price × USDINR × import duty - all three must align to rally.
From 2013 to 2021 jewellery gold returned ~50%, less than a bank FD - hedge, not compounding asset.
Gold hedges inflation and currency risk; with a stable rupee and rising rates expected, the hedge was cheap to skip.
Higher duty widens the smuggling arbitrage; the 2021 cut to 10% narrowed it.
quotes: Gold is for the beauty you enjoy, not the returns you expect.

summary: Bounce: gap-up +100 sustained; first day since the fall that Dow/S&P/Nasdaq were all green. DII +1,700cr vs FII just -50cr; broad-based rally (all sectors, mid/small caps) with VIX -9%. Reprises the expiry-day-SIP edge (volatile months close at series lows → next series' first session bounces). Bull-market correction anatomy: Jan 14,800→13,600 pre-budget then +2,000; ICICI -15-20% in the recent leg. Golden rule: 'people lose money because they do not want to lose money.'
lessons: Capitulation lows followed by DII absorption + broad-based green breadth = correction exhausting.
SIP on expiry day beats SIP on the 5th because expiry-day closes skew low in volatile series.

summary: Maharashtra COVID restrictions triggered knee-jerk Monday selloff: Nifty -400, Bank Nifty -1,500 intraday, India VIX +15% at worst; markets recovered 200+ points intraday. Speaker called it an overreaction given vaccine availability and strong US jobs (+916k).
lessons: Markets move violently only on surprise news; the same shock repeated gets a muted reaction.
In hedged positions, square off the sold leg's offset first - unwinding in the wrong order makes the short naked and margin explodes.

summary: Election-day special: TMC landslide in West Bengal against exit polls; DMK leading TN. US barred Indian travellers from May 4; FII −₹3,500 cr Friday after rally to 15,050. April GST ₹1.41 lakh cr all-time record (+20% MoM) despite COVID. Sputnik V landed; 18–45 vaccination opened. Calls > puts now (14,800/15,000 walls). Range ~14,200–15,000.
lessons: A record tax collection during the worst health month is the economy's tell — separate the health cycle from the economy.
Sentiment flip visible in OI: unwinding 14,900/15,000 puts + adding 14,800–15,000 calls = resistance building into strength.

summary: Post-election Monday: SGX -250 gap-down bought; Nifty briefly green then faded; Reliance (-6% post-results), IndusInd and Kotak all fell on results; Sun TV -7% into F&O ban (forced-square-off dynamics, not fundamentals: 'staring-contest' ban mechanics). PowerGrid InvIT ~5x oversubscribed. Full collateral vs haircut explainer (10% MF haircut; 50% cash rule economics).
lessons: F&O-banned stocks trade on forced square-offs, not fundamentals - ignore the price action, keep the long-term thesis.
Haircut (SEBI-mandated) and 100% collateral are different things; the 50% cash rule makes pledge-only trading impossible at most brokers.

summary: Sponsored explainer of theme-based basket investing: curated stock baskets by theme (rural demand, dividend yield, all-weather), one-click execution, periodic rebalancing, SIP support, and costs vs mutual funds and DIY buying.
lessons: Theme baskets let you express a macro view (good monsoon -> rural demand -> FMCG and two-wheelers) more precisely than a mutual fund.
All-weather allocation pairs equity with debt (stability) and gold (inverse correlation) as a built-in hedge.
Rebalancing keeps a basket true to its thesis - weight shifts or constituent swaps are decided by rule, not emotion.
Direct stock-picking for novices is the ladies-finger problem: self-selection picks the worst ones; curated baskets or funds reduce it.
quotes: Trading is for making money. Investment is for creating wealth.
Gold is usually inversely correlated with equity market. So it is a hedge to each other.

summary: Anti-hype episode: 500%-in-2-months is a clickbait debunk; the Zerodha-founder anecdote (₹2L→₹2cr election bet, then full loss in 6 months), margin math proving ₹3L cannot trade 20 lots, and the greed-stimulation formula behind ultra-high-return claims.
lessons: A ₹2-lakh election lottery that became ₹2 crore ended as a total loss within 6 months — luck is not a system.
₹3 lakh capital cannot carry 20 lots: exposure margin alone ran ~₹20,000 per lot — the arithmetic exposes fake claims.
Anyone promising 500–10,000% should accept your capital on a profit-share instead of charging fees — they never do.
Small-capital traders are the target demographic of return-claim scams.
quotes: If a gambler never wins, the casino closes — the occasional win is what keeps gamblers losing.
To cheat someone, first stimulate his greed.

summary: How Indians can access US equities: LRS forbids offshore derivatives, cash equity allowed but shares are expensive; proposes an ETF-based global allocation (half India, half NASDAQ) that doubles as a rupee-depreciation hedge.
lessons: Indian tax residents cannot trade derivatives in any foreign market under LRS - cash equity is the legal route.
US mega-cap share prices (lakhs per share) lock out small investors; index ETFs solve ticket-size and selection risk.
A US allocation is a natural hedge: if the rupee depreciates, dollar assets gain even when the share price is flat.
Splitting equity 50% India / 50% NASDAQ 100, with the India half split across large- and next-50 index ETFs, balances beta.

strategies.construction: 50% Indian equity ETFs (25% Nifty 50 ETF + 25% Nifty Next 50 ETF) + 50% NASDAQ 100 ETF; SIP-able; quarterly rebalance
strategies.numbers: minimum ticket ~1,509 rupees; claimed 8.5% in first 5 months
