strategies.risks: US drawdowns, no derivatives hedging allowed offshore

quotes: The power of the crocodile is only inside the water - we understand our companies better than any foreigner does.

summary: Recovered 90 pts from gap-down, held 15,800 till 12:30, then Europe-triggered slide (Dow futures -150 to -500; 800 Dow pts in 2 sessions); HDFC twins >1/3 of Nifty fall; top-5 stocks >60% of fall; FIIs -2,199cr vs DIIs +1,048cr; 6 weeks of FII selling, Nifty just -50 from 11 Jun; UK Delta >50,000/day; Adani: ministry told Parliament SEBI investigating group companies + frozen-accounts flip-flop saga; Indian Bank result +3.5%; range 15,500-16,000 for 6-7 weeks.
lessons: Global falls hit all markets, but relative damage depends on the local cycle (India was post-wave-2).
Bad news arrives in bunches - a pessimistic pre-results setup is actually favorable for positive surprises.

summary: Expects 17,000 resistance; 16,800-put sellers safe until ~17,050-17,100. Reviews event-reaction history (2004 election -30%, 2009 +20%, 2016 Trump, 2020 Biden, budget 2021 +1,500). China PMI 50.1 mild drag; GDP ~20% expected on low base; HDFC put-selling idea; range 16,880-17,020.
lessons: Markets make bigger moves just before or just after major events; the drift often continues both sides of the event.
Opposite-of-consensus option selling near resistance needs the collected premium buffer (strike + premium math).

summary: Violent Wednesday-style churn a day early: Bank Nifty -500/+600/-300, Nifty 17,420→17,300→+150→-75, closing just -15. HDFC +₹100 from intraday low saved the index. FII -₹145 cr, DII -₹136 cr (small). 17,400 straddle paid despite chaos. Warning: huge volatility at ATH can mark a short-term top; confirmation needs 2-3 sessions. Teases a non-market learning series.
lessons: Markets tend to top with rising volatility; bottom too - but after a 7,500→17,500 run, top volatility is the risk to respect.
A single heavyweight gap-up (HDFC +100) can neutralise a whole sector's drag - contribution accounting is the daily edge.

summary: Pre-2022-budget crypto tax explainer: investor (few trades/yr) taxed as capital gains vs trader (hundreds of trades) as business income; crypto trading is not 'speculative'; mining is a business with deductible expenses; asset-declaration thresholds explained.
lessons: Frequency decides classification: a few crypto trades a year is investing (capital gains); hundreds is trading (business income).
Crypto trading is not speculative income — you receive actual tokens, unlike F&O — so business-expense deductions apply.
Mining is a business: electricity and incidentals are deductible, computers depreciated as capital assets.
Taxable income above ₹50 lakh requires ITR-2 asset disclosures, including crypto holdings bought with rupees (not 'foreign assets').
quotes: If you buy and sell hundreds of times a year, you are not an investor — you are a trader, and crypto trading is as good as trading in futures and options.

summary: Argues Oct-Nov 2021's India-specific FII selloff (₹20,000cr in 8-9 sessions, timed block prints) was an FII-government tax standoff, not a global event. Historical arc: 2014 unkept corporate-tax promise → 2019 FPI surcharge → withdrawal plus surprise 30%-to-22% cut. Also the IRCTC convenience-fee fiasco.
lessons: Institutions slice large sales through the day; sudden 200+ point prints signal deliberate signals, not natural flow.
India-specific falls happen only around FPI taxation disputes — three such episodes in 15 years, each resolved by government climb-down.
Policy u-turns (announce Monday, withdraw Tuesday) cost credibility and market cap far exceeding the revenue sought.
A correct macro thesis can still lose money when government intervention breaks the transmission (crude-down OMC trade).
quotes: Taxation should be like a honeybee taking honey from the flower — not like juice crushed out of sugarcane, again and again, till the last drop.

summary: Macro triage for late 2021: (1) Baltic Dry Index's 50% one-month fall is mean reversion after a 100% spike, not a demand collapse; (2) farm-law repeal mirrors 2018-19 — FII selling on election fear flips to buying when the ruling party's odds improve (₹75,000cr sold in six months); (3) Europe's COVID wave — aftershock framework: wave 1 −40%, wave 2 −10%, wave 3 −5%.
lessons: Freight and commodity indices spike and mean-revert — a 50% fall after a 100% spike is noise, not a demand signal.
Every indicator reads two ways (high inflation = pricing power or overheating); context picks the reading.
FII flows track election odds: 2018-19 they sold on hung-parliament fear until a geopolitical event flipped sentiment — watch state-election season the same way.
Shocks decay geometrically: wave 1 −40%, wave 2 −10%, wave 3 −5% — 'markets don't react twice for the same reason' means smaller, not zero.
quotes: An earthquake of magnitude eight is followed by aftershocks — four, then one, then half. Wave one fell 40%, wave two 10%, wave three will be 5%.

summary: Opening rally fully sold: Nifty -300 from high, Bank Nifty -700; blames FII selling not Omicron. FIIs sold ₹3356 cr, DIIs only ₹1649 cr. Heavy call writing at 17500 but 17000PE still max OI. He sold 17500 short straddle @600. Flagged LIC IPO (10% policyholder reservation), UP elections and budget as upcoming uncertainty.
lessons: Watch index heavyweights (HDFC twins) to detect institutional selling in real time.
Secondary-market selling to fund primary-market IPO applications rarely makes sense vs comparable valuations.

summary: Frames relentless FII selling (~95,000 crore since April 2021) as a war between foreign portfolio investors and the government over retro-tax reassessment notices, replaying the 2019 FPI surcharge episode that ended only with the 30%-to-22% corporate tax cut.
lessons: Institutional selling driven by policy hostility ends with a government concession - watch tax-policy news as the release valve.
Retail demat growth and SIP flows have become a counterweight able to absorb record FII selling.
In a two-way whipsaw regime, both option buyers and sellers get chopped; sit out until one side stops.
quotes: If you ask me to explain in one sentence what has been happening in the last two months, it is a war between government and FPIs.

summary: Powerful short covering: Nifty +300, Bank Nifty +1000; 1,200-pt swing in 4 sessions (4,000+ in Bank Nifty). First day with zero intraday selling: FIIs -₹579 cr, DIIs +₹1735 cr. Thesis: structural bull run - no 10% correction in years outside COVID/Lehman; retail has switched to the DII side (three-rowdy paradigm). China comparison: 2008 both ~6000; now India 18,000 vs China 3,500. Stays bullish.
lessons: Retail is the swing voter: aligned with DIIs, not FIIs, it now sets the market's direction.
A 10% index correction is historically rare outside systemic crises - treat it as accumulation territory.

summary: Fourth straight down day; a 2:35pm basket sell took Nifty -100 and Bank Nifty -250 in 55 minutes. FIIs -₹3400 cr, DIIs +₹1500 cr; December: every session a sell day, >₹23,000 cr MTD (Oct ~25,000, Nov ~40,000 per speaker). Rupee 76.23 among multi-year lows - repatriation evidence. Crypto bill postponed to next Parliament session after a 20% India-crypto crash (even USDT) on mere statements. Fed verdict tonight; 17300 the new fight; survival = sell calls into 100-pt spikes.
lessons: Late-session basket orders mark institutional programs - the last hour often carries the whole day's story.
A depreciating currency during selling confirms repatriation, not rotation.

summary: Year-ahead 2022 outlook: 2021 scoreboard, the crash-rebound asymmetry (only two 100%-plus years, both after 40-50% crashes), a VIX-implied 15,000-21,000 range monetized with a long-dated strangle, FII-selling-vs-SIP absorption math, and the 2022 event map: budget, five state elections, Fed taper and rate hikes.
lessons: Crash depth sets rebound height: 100%+ index years occurred only after 40-50% crashes, so deep-fall years are the rebound candidates.
Long-dated wide strangles monetize the VIX-implied annual range without intraday stress.
Domestic SIP flows (~1.2 lakh crore/year) can mathematically absorb another year of record FII selling.
Six months before a general election, state-election results act as FII sentiment catalysts (2018-19 precedent).

strategies.name: Long-dated Nifty short strangle (annual range)
strategies.construction: Sold December-2022 15,000 put and 21,000 call
strategies.numbers: Combined premium ~700 points (~35,000 per lot); margin ~1.8 lakh initially, easing to 80-90k later; already ~100 points in profit at recording
strategies.best_regime: Wide VIX-implied annual range with no intent to predict direction
strategies.adjustments: None needed unless a boundary approaches; long-dated structure ignores short-term news
strategies.risks: Both sides breached in an extreme year; margin lock-up for 12 months

quotes: If you drop a ball from a very high place, when it touches the ground the rebounding is also very high.

summary: FIIs turned buyers in four of five sessions (only the Fed balance-sheet-news day saw Rs 1,900 crore selling) and Bank Nifty exploded +2,250 vs Nifty's +460; ICICI/HDFC ADRs up ~2-2.6%; Wednesday flagged as a six-event collision day (US CPI, India CPI, IIP, TCS/Infosys/Wipro results); OI range 17,500-18,000 expected to break; state-election counting on a working day removes gap risk for option sellers.
lessons: When many binary events collide on one day, clear overnight positions — the gap, not the outcome, is the risk.
FII buying resumption shows up first in banks and rate-sensitives; that is where the beta is.

summary: India decoupled from jittery US: Infosys and TCS rallied post-results (opposite of last quarter); HDFC Bank posted ~18% profit growth (near pre-COVID 20%); result-day price action framed as 'who blinks first' between longs and shorts; ~20% of Nifty-50 results land next week across nine sectors; pre-budget optimism ahead of five state elections.
lessons: Result-day price action is decided by positioning (longs vs shorts 'blinking first'); fundamentals get priced over the following days.
FII selling concentrates in specific heavyweights (HDFC Bank) — their short-covering is the fastest index fuel.

summary: Post-crash reset: US futures recovering; India results strong (RIL O2C +56%, ICICI +25% profit, HDFC Bank +18%, JSW blockbuster) vs FII selling ~3–5k cr/day; DII buying the only question; pre-budget rally historically absent then post-budget surge.
lessons: Watch the DII response to FII selling, not the selling itself — April 2021 precedent shows heavy selling with a rising tape
Fear peaks before the event; 'sell on bad news, buy on news' applies on the downside too

summary: Pre-budget policy letter: STT history (introduced 2004 in lieu of LTCG; LTCG reinstated 2018 while STT stayed - double taxation), option STT raised five-fold, FII selling near 1.75 lakh crore since April 2021 absorbed by retail SIPs, peak-margin penalty critique via snake/rat parables, and GIFT City parity for resident taxpayers.
lessons: STT is unique in taxing losers - no other business taxes you for losing money; it was meant to replace LTCG, which returned in 2018 anyway.
A tax deducted at source offsets final tax liability; treating it as a mere expense changes the math (100 income: TDS route costs 20, expense route 27).
Retail flows - record SIPs, demat accounts, IPO subscriptions - absorbed FII selling that once would have crashed the Sensex.
Well-intended rules (peak margin penalty) get weaponized by brokers as blanket deductions - good intentions, bad transmission.
quotes: FIIs are like our wife - sometimes you hate, sometimes you love, but you cannot live without her.
Call it securities transaction punishment: it is the only place in India where you pay tax for losing money.

summary: Asia overreacted: SGX -400 but opened -200; fall to near prior low then DII-led recovery; Dow futures +600 off lows. PSU bank index +5%; HDFC twins + IT dragged (TCS, Infosys, Reliance = half the Nifty fall). India VIX 21, US VIX >30. Budget hope framed via corporate-tax-cut precedent.
lessons: US VIX above 30 is a danger zone; comfort returns only below 25.
A surprise positive budget (like the 2019 tax cut) can kill shorts overnight.

summary: US GDP 6.9% spark: Dow swung -400 to +600 to flat (~1,600-pt range). Tesla -11% on results; Apple +5% after-hours. Crude higher; rupee down ~1 in days. FIIs sold 13,000+ cr over two sessions (~$2B); DIIs defend 17,000. Expect consolidation 16,850-17,300 until budget; bullish after.
lessons: FIIs sell more aggressively toward expiry and on expiry day.
Oversold market + likely-good budget (five state elections pending) could repeat the 2021 post-budget rally.

summary: Post-Fed volatility persisted (Dow ±1,000 daily) with US VIX stuck above 30 for eight sessions before a 9% Friday drop; India decoupled on strong results — PSU banks surged, IndusInd +36% profit; FIIs set a record (15,000 crore over three sessions) with no local trigger; Budget Tuesday seen as the sentiment reset, needed for the 1-lakh-crore LIC IPO to sail through.
lessons: India VIX falling on a big red day signals downside exhaustion — writers are not pricing escalation.
A mega-IPO on the calendar gives the government a reason to engineer sentiment; budget expectations follow.

summary: Nasdaq +6% in two sessions (Netflix/Tesla +10% days); US VIX -20% in two days; SGX +400 toward 17,500. FIIs sold <5,000 cr Monday, DIIs matched. January selling 41,000+ cr (~$6B, highest post-COVID). Budget tomorrow: VIX expected to crash; FII index-futures long only ~32%.
lessons: Budget-day moves are about positioning, not budget content - 'who blinks first'.
FOMO will eventually force heavy short-sellers to buy back higher.

summary: Budget-eve: gap-up ~200-300 to 17,600, Bank Nifty near 39,000; budget read as 'nothing negative' - ITC up on no tobacco tax. Post-budget FII basket selling: Nifty -400 intraday, Bank Nifty -1,100, then recovery. FIIs 3,624 cr sold; 5th straight day >3,000 cr. PSU bank index first red close; bond yields up post-budget.
lessons: No negative news is positive news.
When price direction, VIX crush and time decay all align, option sellers have their best day.

summary: Budget-day trade log (recorded then shown live): with US VIX under 25 and Nifty already corrected from 18,600 to 17,300, sold a Nifty put ladder (weekly 17,000-16,600; monthly 16,500-16,000), a Bank Nifty put ladder (36,500-36,000), put ratios (buy 17,600PE/sell 2x 17,300PE; buy 39,000PE/sell 2x 38,000PE), and 30%-stop-loss short straddles (BN 38,600; Nifty 17,500). Intraday P&L ~3.4 lakh, net ~27 lakh.
lessons: Enter binary events with low expectations after a correction - downside surprise is then limited.
US VIX below 25 is a permission slip for premium selling into the event.
Sell far out-of-the-money puts where hedgers and margin-traders create double demand.
Straddle stop-loss rule: 30% of one side's premium; if one side is stopped, move the other side's stop to cost - max loss equals one side's 30%.

strategies.name: Nifty/Bank Nifty put ladders into budget
strategies.construction: Weekly puts 17,000-16,600 (Nifty); monthly 16,500-16,000; Bank Nifty 36,500-36,000 (all sold)
strategies.numbers: Far-OTM premiums 20-134 rupees; ~2,500 rupees per 100 captured vs ~1-1.5 lakh margin (~2.5% in 2-3 sessions)
strategies.best_regime: Bullish-to-neutral into an event after a correction, with global VIX subdued
strategies.adjustments: Hedge sold at 38,300 put for the positional book; no stops on far ladders
strategies.risks: Genuine crash blows through all sold strikes

strategies.construction: Buy 1x 17,600 PE, sell 2x 17,300 PE (Nifty); buy 39,000 PE, sell 2x 38,000 PE (Bank Nifty)
strategies.numbers: Both roughly cost-neutral (~263 vs 2x135; ~900 vs 2x450)

strategies.risks: Sharp fall below the short strike creates double downside

strategies.construction: Sell BN 38,600 CE+PE (~1,400 combined); sell Nifty 17,500 CE+PE (~450 combined)
strategies.numbers: 30% stop on each side; after one stop hits, other side revised to cost
strategies.best_regime: Post-event IV collapse with no big directional move
strategies.adjustments: Stop-and-cost-revision rule
strategies.risks: Whipsaw triggers both sides in a trending budget reaction

summary: Post-budget session aftermath: Bank Nifty fell ~1,100 points intraday then fully recovered; India VIX dropped ~9-10%; the day's book showed ~78-82 lakh profit (about 3% of a 25-crore capital base). Core lessons: post-event IV collapse cuts premiums on both sides, rewarding pre-budget sellers; HNI behavior - huge capital, no greed, 30-40% per annum ambitions; 2% per month compounding path to 100 crore.
lessons: After a big event, implied volatility collapses - both calls and puts deflate; pre-event sellers collect from the IV crush.
Carrying positions through an event requires capital cushion and acceptance of intraday whipsaws (Bank Nifty -1,100 then full recovery).
Return framing: an 80-lakh day is 3% of capital - absolute profit without ROI context misleads.
Target 30-40% per annum, not 100% days; collateral yield (6-7%) plus trading return compounds toward wealth.
quotes: People want to get rich quick, and in that process they become poor quick.
We sell the business, not the dream - we are not dream merchants.

summary: Budget-day rally extended: opened +120, ran past 17,600 (Bank Nifty ~39,000); afternoon FII basket selling (-400 Nifty, -1,100 Bank Nifty) then DII/Europe-led recovery. FIIs ~183 cr, DIIs +425 cr. India VIX -6.6% below 19. 17,700 put OI / 18,000 call - range 17,700-18,000. PSU bank index first red close.
lessons: When FII selling pauses, FII-favourite counters (HDFC twins, Kotak, ICICI) rally first.
Three aligned forces - direction, VIX crush, time decay - make the option seller's day.

summary: Compounding sermon: 2% per month (24% p.a.) doubles capital roughly every 3 years via rule of 72 - 1 lakh becomes 10 crore in 30 years; 10 lakh becomes 100 crore. Frames an 84-lakh profit day as 3% of a 25-crore capital (ROI over absolutes, beggar-vs-Ambani ROI joke), cites broker statistics (99% never beat FD returns over 3 years; 90% lose 90% in 90 sessions), and names consistency and income tax as the only caveats.
lessons: 2% per month, compounded, doubles capital every ~3 years: 1 lakh to 10 crore, or 10 lakh to 100 crore, in 30 years.
Judge returns as ROI, not absolute profit - a big rupee day can be a small percentage of capital.
The market inverts greed: those chasing quick riches become poor quick and enrich patient, capitalized participants.
Industry stats cited by brokers: 99% of traders never beat bank FD returns over 3 years; 90% lose 90% of capital in 90 sessions.
quotes: People want to get rich quick, and in that process they become poor quick - and make patient people richer.
Mukesh Ambani's ROI is 10-15-20%. A beggar's ROI is infinity. Who is the better businessman?

summary: Post-budget surge (17,100→17,800) interrupted by Meta's -25%; 1,000-point Nifty swing in five sessions; weekend results beat (SBI +62% profit, BoB strong); heavy monthly put writing at 17,500 read as writer conviction that the bottom holds; RBI Wednesday a likely non-event (reverse repo +20bp); US CPI now matters more than India's; range 17,400-18,000.
lessons: VIX cooling is the option writer's party — premium collapse after event risk pays the patient seller.
When monthly puts pile up at a level, that strike becomes a defended floor; respect it until proven broken.

summary: Post-Budget-2022 explainer of India's new digital-asset tax regime: flat 30% on gains, no expense deduction, no basic exemption, 1% TDS per transaction, gifts taxed in recipient's hands, effective FY2022-23 from 1 April 2022.
lessons: India's 30% flat crypto tax with no expense deduction or basic exemption makes frequent trading structurally penalized, not just taxed.
1% TDS per transaction means a daily crypto trader effectively ties up 365% of turnover in TDS until refund season.
Crypto losses cannot be set off against any other income; gifts of crypto are taxed 30% in the recipient's hands.
quotes: You have to pay flat 30% tax... you cannot show any expenses. Even the brokerage cannot be shown as expense.

summary: US CPI shocked at 7.5% (vs 7.2% expected) then Russia-Ukraine invasion intelligence (dated by 20 February) knocked Dow -1,000 in two days; India had moved opposite (bad start, dovish-RBI Thursday); uncertainty declared the market's poison for a month (Fed, elections, LIC IPO, crude >$95); speaker hedged longs with 17,500-17,700 call writes; 17,000 monthly put highest OI; 16,800 (200-DMA) the next support.
lessons: Markets can absorb good or bad news but not uncertainty — announced threat dates get deferred while guard drops, then strike.
Writing calls against long holdings is portfolio insurance, not a trade — cap upside to cushion the fall.
When CPI misses to the upside, the rate-hike repricing hits banks and growth stocks hardest within days.

summary: Fell 200, rallied 250 after 1:30pm, then a 2:30pm NATO troop-buildup claim erased it within an hour (Bank Nifty -450, Nifty -200). LIC IPO dates announced (Mar 10-14) clashing with five-state election results day. FIIs -1,890 cr, DIIs +1,180 cr.
lessons: In event weeks a 600-point index swing can reverse within one hour - near-expiry option selling becomes Russian roulette.
A headline that barely moves the origin country's market but crashes yours signals local positioning, not fundamentals.

summary: Certain vs uncertain uncertainties: dated events (budget, election results) are tradable risk; Russia-Ukraine is not. Worst US night of 2022 (Dow -600, Nasdaq -3%) then recovery on talks; green-hydrogen policy hopes lift RIL; HDFC holding green in a crash flags bottoming.
lessons: Trade known-date events; stand aside from open-ended uncertainty.
A stock holding firm while its market crashes shows accumulation strength.

summary: Opened -350 (vs SGX -200) with the first decisive 200-DMA break in ~2 years, then a +350 recovery; Russia recovered from -8/9% as its VIX fell 96 to 82; India VIX up a 4th straight day, intraday ~28. Recovery on bad news = bottom signal; 16,800 double bottom.
lessons: A market that rallies on bad news has found its bottom - that low becomes the reference.
Exit all short-premium positions if VIX crosses 30; election weeks are the only exception.

summary: War day: Nifty fell about 900 points (roughly 1,000 from the prior close), Bank Nifty about 2,000; 200-DMA and the 16,400 swing low both broke. India VIX closed decisively above 30 (US ~37, Russia ~127). Advice: flat until clarity; long-term staged entries begin.
lessons: VIX above 30 means flat: no positions, no exceptions except election weeks.
Near a bottom, stage entries in 20-25% tranches instead of calling the exact low.

summary: War day 11: Europe -4% Friday (Italy -12%, Germany -10% weekly) while US saved by strong jobs and record-low unemployment. Author turning bearish; market has fallen Lehman/COVID-scale 15-20%, down-circuit risk flagged. State-election exit polls next day (UP decisive). Hedge, don't naked-short.
lessons: In a fragile market good news goes unreacted while bad news crashes it - the opposite of a bull run.
Indiscriminate shorting is dangerous: 2009 election results produced a 20% gap-up against crowded shorts.

summary: Fantastic rally: Nifty 15,700→16,400+ (+700) as Zelensky's NATO climbdown, Russian 'not overthrowing government' line, halted Poland jet transfer, and ceasefire corridors aligned. Opened 180-200 points above SGX - DII/LIC-type support. FIIs still sold 4,818 crore; March heading past the 65,000-crore record. Election-counting roller coaster tomorrow.
lessons: When the last bull turns bear, markets bottom - his own public bearish turn preceded the relief rally by a day.
Opening 180-200 points above SGX with no news = domestic quasi-sovereign support absorbing supply; watch who buys, not just what rises.

summary: Global relief rally: Germany +8%; UAE agreed to raise crude output; Brent 130→110-111. Reliance +5.5% on GRM ~$16 vs $10 (potential +60% refining profitability) but OI fell 3% - short covering, not fresh longs. Nov-2018 parallel: BJP lost 5 state elections then FIIs sold Nov 21 2018-Feb 2019. UP results today.
lessons: Price up + OI down = short covering, not fresh conviction - do not extrapolate such moves.
Read-through trades (Singapore GRM → Reliance margins) work only when the market has risk appetite to price them.

summary: Election-day pattern: strong first half, sold in the second. Nifty 15,700→16,750 in two sessions (+1,050), Bank Nifty +3,000; afternoon sell-off (-300/-1,000) met renewed short covering - a FII-vs-DII fight. BJP won 4 of 5 states incl. UP (30-40 seats fewer). Turkey FM talks yielded nothing; US CPI 7.9% (40-yr high) due.
lessons: Election-day tape has a shape: conviction rallies into results get sold once uncertainty resolves - fade the first-half euphoria on result days.
Bear-market rallies are fast, uniform, and sold into - the +8% Germany day was half-given-back within 24 hours.

summary: Earnings-week IT strategy ahead of TCS results (11-Apr) and Infosys (13-Apr). Context: TCS range 3,400-4,000 (Jan high on 4,000 buyback news; Ukraine-war gap to 3,400; pre-result dip to 3,650); Accenture's strong print is a read-through. Executed structure: buy 1x 3,600 CE, sell 3x 3,800 CE, buy 2x 4,000 CE, sell 2x 3,400 PE, buy 2x 3,200 PE - a ratio spread with both wings capped; margin cut from ~Rs.2 lakh to ~Rs.1.22 lakh, max profit ~Rs.30,000 near a 3,800 close, POP ~68%, breakevens 3,400-3,900, max loss ~Rs.59,000.
lessons: Same-business read-throughs work: Accenture's results telegraph Indian IT results ('same people, same mindset').
A call ratio is safe only with a capped upside wing - and capping also slashes margin.
Wing both sides around the earnings range: sold 3,400 PE anchored on the 3,400 war-low support.
Strategy strikes should come from the stock's own range map (buyback level, war gap, consolidation), not hope.

strategies.name: TCS earnings call-ratio with double caps (iron-fly-like credit structure)
strategies.construction: Buy 1x 3,600 CE; sell 3x 3,800 CE; buy 2x 4,000 CE; sell 2x 3,400 PE; buy 2x 3,200 PE (10 lots total, basket order at market)

strategies.best_regime: Earnings week with an expected favorable result but capped macro upside (war + Fed overhang)
strategies.adjustments: Exit or run to expiry based on Tuesday's gap reaction; update promised on close
strategies.risks: Gap beyond 3,900 breaks the call wing; below 3,400 the put wing bleeds; earnings gaps are binary

quotes: Who said option selling is only for rich people? With structured strategies, even small capital works.

summary: Dow -2000 from Thursday afternoon to Monday - matched only by Lehman, COVID, Feb-2018 (same inflation trigger; India added LTCG budget double whammy, Nifty fell ~700 then). 2018 pattern: 2000-pt low held 10-15 sessions then broke. Shorts built this time -> cushioning short-covering. SGX -200; May future <17000. ICICI results decent; Reliance called off Future deal; HDFC Bank record dividend; US crude <$100, Brent $104.
lessons: Crash path-dependence: when shorts are built during the fall, the bounce gets a short-covering cushion (Feb 2018 fell with no shorts, so it didn't bounce)
Each retest weakens a support; closing-basis break is the real trigger

summary: Brief explainer of presumptive taxation: no books of accounts or bills needed; a fixed share of turnover (6% as stated) is deemed profit and taxed without further questions.
lessons: Presumptive taxation trades documentation burden for a deemed profit percentage on turnover.

summary: Rupee panic past 81 plus the UK mini-budget (sterling at record lows, DXY 112) triggered a thousand-point Sensex/Bank Nifty fall; 17,400 support broke and 'all hell broke loose'; he squared puts, sold calls 17,500-18,300; September 2022 likened to September 2008.
lessons: Rupee depreciation is a double whammy for FIIs (mark-to-market plus conversion loss) - currency crashes convert into equity selling.
In panic, hedged call-selling with far-put margin offsets is the conservative posture; going net short options still needs stop discipline.

summary: US closed higher despite strong jobs; China reaffirmed zero-COVID, Apple warned on supply - US futures lower. SBI results 'very good'; author's PSU Bank BeES +30% in under a year. Resistance 18,300-18,400; December target 18,500-19,000. Flags December black swans: US CPI, Fed, Gujarat election (2017 flashback: first-round Congress lead dropped Nifty 400-500, BJP lead recovered all).
lessons: State elections in the ruling party's home turf move the index through the BJP-win proxy - position for the result round, not the exit poll.
Nifty has not crossed 18,400 all year - a level tested that often is either a wall or a launchpad; flows decide which.

summary: Midterm day: US higher ahead of results; author's rule - 'you can predict anything except election results' (Brexit flashback). China CPI better; SGX ~18,400; Nifty and Bank Nifty ~200-300 from all-time highs, needing IT and PSU banks to carry. Trade ideas: Manappuram Finance long (stop 100, sell 100 puts), India Cements long above 251 (stop 240); 18,000 PE huge OI into Tuesday expiry.
lessons: Never carry heavy positions into election results - polls are opinions, outcomes are coin flips (Brexit lesson).
When a stock has corrected ~50% and its business driver (gold price) has turned, selling puts with a stop is a defined-risk revival trade.

summary: US fell >2% (Nasdaq, S&P) on midterm run-off uncertainty plus CPI due tonight; SGX 18,130 with ~70-point premium (spot ~18,060); DIIs sold 2-3x FII buying the prior day; crude -3%; support seen at 18,000. Tata Motors and Ashok Leyland results due. OI: 18,000-18,200 range bets; no monthly close above 18,000 since last October - today's expiry could change that.
lessons: Run-off elections convert one-day event risk into a month of uncertainty - uncertainty, not direction, is what markets cannot price.
A spot close above 18,000 for the first monthly close in a year would flip the technical regime.

summary: Debut analysis video: DHFL bond sale panic drags housing finance stocks; speaker argues capitulation marks a bottom and irrational markets reward skilled traders.
lessons: Markets bottom after big panic selling (capitulation); overreaction to one name often marks a multi-week low.
Panic in one bond/stock drags the whole sector down with it - contagion is mechanical, not fundamental.
Traders who understand irrationality can profit during it; accumulation often starts at maximum pessimism.
quotes: When people are optimistic they will pay the price of a diamond for a pebble; when pessimistic, they will not pay the price of a pebble for a diamond.

summary: Panic morning selling found support at 10,900 (62.8% Fibonacci retracement and Friday low); Nifty shot up 180 points. IndiaBulls Housing Finance crashed ~20% on IL&FS crisis, then rebounded 100+ after IL&FS chairman said all options open to revive it. Bank Nifty swung 10% intraday.
lessons: Markets often bottom after a day of extreme volatility combined with a double bottom.

summary: RBI-government standoff (Section 7, governor resignation reports) knocked Nifty to 10,100; Coal India FPO (4,500cr + 9,000cr greenshoe) added supply. Government clarification fueled short covering: Nifty +300, Bank Nifty +600 from lows; HDFC Bank +5%. India VIX crashed 14% intraday. FII sold only 193cr; DII bought 1,120cr.
lessons: Max-OI put strikes show option sellers' conviction levels about support.

summary: Trump's 10% tariff tweet on Chinese phones hit Apple after-hours; Nifty low 10,585, then US-China 'agreed to solve the trade war' headlines lifted US futures and Nifty 70-80 points. HDFC Bank pushed Bank Nifty to a 3-month swing high. OI: 26,000 PE / 26,500 CE. Nifty expiry favored toward the top of 10,500-10,800.
lessons: Trade-war headlines move index futures within minutes - fade confirmation, not the first headline.

summary: Foundational primer: calls and puts taught through a Virat Kohli cricket-betting analogy and a business-profit story; explains strike, premium, expiry and how expectation moves premium before price does.
lessons: An option is asymmetric betting: buyer risks only the premium; seller pays 1:1 per point beyond the strike.
Premium moves on expectation, not just price - a batter racing toward a century raises the 'premium' before the century exists.
Call buyers profit when market rises, put buyers when it falls - but volatility and time decay can still turn a right view into a loss.
Buyers can exit before expiry; profit-taking need not wait for settlement.
quotes: The expectation will shoot up... though he has not hit the century, the premium rises as he scores more runs.

summary: Systematic demolition of the three buyer advantages (low premium, limited risk, unlimited reward): collateral funding, 20% win probability, profit-booking dilemma, and the lottery/robbery framing of risk-reward-probability.
lessons: 'Limited risk, unlimited reward' always pairs with very low probability (lottery) or very high risk (robbery).
Seller's real risk is bounded by the trading capital actually deployed, not theoretical unlimited loss.
Buyer psychology fails at profit booking - 10 to 50 to zero on expiry day; seller's capped profit removes greed.
Nifty never moves far enough in a month for 'unlimited' to matter; few hundred points is the real range.
quotes: Every day I switch on TV, I find some people die of accidents. Are we going to say getting out of the house is unlimited risk?
The probability of winning for an option buyer is less than 20%.

summary: VIX masterclass during COVID: definition (expected 30-day movement, not a fear gauge that must rise in falls), sqrt-12 monthly conversion, advance-decline check for why VIX fell on a falling day, and strike placement beyond the expected move.
lessons: VIX measures expected one-month movement; it can fall in a falling market when the fall is narrow (heavyweights only, breadth positive).
Monthly expected move = VIX / sqrt(12); place short strikes beyond that band (example: VIX 60 -> ~17% band).
VIX is derived from option prices - the straddle premium is a live cross-check of the VIX-implied range.
High VIX favors sellers who keep distance; low VIX means the market is priced for calm and strikes must come closer.

strategies.name: VIX-based expected-move strangle placement
strategies.construction: Sell puts below spot - (VIX/sqrt(12))% and calls above spot + (VIX/sqrt(12))%
strategies.numbers: VIX 60 -> monthly band ~17.3%; spot 8,000 -> sell puts below ~6,500, calls above ~9,500; May 8,000 straddle ~1,600 (~20% for 37 trading days)
strategies.best_regime: Elevated VIX (crisis); recompute daily as VIX moves
strategies.adjustments: None stated - guideline framing, refresh band as VIX changes
strategies.risks: Band is statistical, not a wall; theta/other factors shift premiums; violent moves can exceed the band

quotes: It is not necessary that when the market goes down, the VIX has to go up - VIX is all about the perception of the market over the next one month.

summary: First-ever Week Ahead video: 3-session COVID holiday week; India VIX falling; Friday's terrible US jobs data moved Dow only -300 (selling exhaustion); HDFC/ICICI ADRs -8% warn of weak Tuesday open; range 7,500-8,500.
lessons: When bad news moves markets less and less, selling is exhausting - negative impact is limited.
ADR moves of index heavyweights preview Indian bank stocks after holidays.

summary: Explains the violent up-move anomaly: strangle sellers trapped by a ~10% rally are forced to buy back far puts to free margin and re-sell closer strikes - creating put-premium distortion. Never deploy all margin; short strangle is the most dangerous strategy.
lessons: In violent moves, premiums behave abnormally because losing-side sellers are forced to square up and roll - not because the market 'should' behave that way.
Never deploy all margin in a strangle; spare cash lets you sell closer strikes without buying back the far leg at the worst price.
Short strangle is called the most dangerous strategy - unlimited one-sided loss with both legs naked.
Margin-release mechanics (square far leg, sell nearer leg) explain bid-ask distortions during panics.

strategies.name: Strangle roll-under-stress mechanics
strategies.construction: Short 9,000CE + 7,000PE written Friday around spot 8,000; on a violent rally, buy back 7,000PE (releasing margin) and sell 7,500/8,000PE instead
strategies.numbers: Legs 1,000 points either side of spot; roll targets 500-1,000 points closer
strategies.best_regime: After violent directional moves when the losing leg must be repositioned
strategies.adjustments: Roll the losing short leg closer using either spare cash (preferred) or margin released by squaring the far leg
strategies.risks: Forced buyback at inflated premiums; whipsaw if the market reverses immediately

quotes: Always remember, when markets move violently, do not expect option premiums to behave in the normal course.

summary: Against unanimous retail bearishness in COVID: lead-vs-lag indicators, the good/very-good/bad/very-bad news quadrant, consensus danger, efficient markets ('you are last to know'), and why heavy put buying at high premium is a losing game.
lessons: Markets price the lead indicator (next few months) - current bad news is already in the price (efficient market: you are last to know).
Very good news invites profit booking; very bad news invites policy rescue - so both can be sell/buy signals respectively.
Consensus is dangerous: when every retail message is bearish, the short trade is already crowded.
Defensive sectors (FMCG/IT/pharma) can rally through market-worst periods - index-level gloom hides stock-level bull markets.
quotes: Good news is a good news; very good news is a bad news. Bad news is a bad news; very bad news is a good news.
You are the last one to know the fact - whatever is in the public domain is already factored into the market.

summary: COVID-era consolidation: Nifty 8,900-9,100 with heavy volatility; Bank Nifty underperformed. Advance-decline favored advancers despite the fall; VIX rose yet premiums fell (Bank Nifty -400 but weekly 18,000 PE -100). FII AND DII both sold >1,000cr - rare. Weekly OI 8,500 PE / 9,500 CE; monthly support migrating up to 8,200 PE.
lessons: Falling premiums on a down day signal the market does not expect follow-through selling.

summary: P&L transparency episode: ~50% return in six April-2020 sessions driven by VIX collapse 86->50 plus a bullish view; demonstrates position-level losses coexisting with net profit, and strike/expiry diversification; explicitly warns viewers not to copy the risk.
lessons: High-VIX regimes let low-volume sellers earn outsized returns as VIX collapses - the profit engine is vega plus view, not volume.
Spread risk across many strikes (6,500 through 8,500 puts) and multiple expiries (weekly/May/June) - never concentrate one strike.
Position-level losses (up to ~1.75 lakh single positions) coexist with net profit - judge the portfolio, not each leg.
Never copy aggressive sizing: capital and risk appetite differ; matching the trade without matching the capital is ruinous.

strategies.name: Strike-and-expiry put ladder (illustrative, high risk)
strategies.construction: Sold puts at 6,500 / 7,000 / 7,300 / 7,400 / 7,500 / 7,800 / 8,500 across weekly, May and June expiries; small stock-option positions (IndusInd 800 qty @22.52; ~2,300PE on a NBFC stock, 4 lots @220)

strategies.adjustments: Laddered entries across expiries instead of single-strike concentration
strategies.risks: Aggressive directional sizing; a renewed crash through the ladder strikes would produce large losses; explicitly not replicable by retail

quotes: We also lose. What matters is whether, at the end of the day, the profits are more than the losses.
I have sold 6,500, 7,000, 7,500, 7,300, 7,400, 7,800, 8,500 - I spread my risk across strike prices and across expiry dates.

summary: PM announced a further 19-day lockdown. Argues the move was 90% expected, so already priced; SGX Nifty traded ~200 points above the India close; herd put-buyers set up for a premium collapse even if prices fell.
lessons: Markets can absorb good or bad news but not uncertainty; once an outcome is known, clarity itself re-prices risk.
When 90% expect a fall, the fall is already priced - consensus trades usually fail.
Option buyers can be right on direction and still lose when uncertainty resolves and premiums collapse.

strategies.name: Multi-strike, multi-expiry put selling (April 2020)
strategies.construction: Sold put options spread across various strike prices and expiry periods rather than one strike
strategies.numbers: 7500PE sold around Rs.75 during a morning dip; SGX Nifty ~9200 vs ~9000 close
strategies.best_regime: Ultra-bearish consensus with the negative surprise already announced

strategies.risks: Losses if the market breaks below the sold strikes; premium is the cap on profit

quotes: Markets can take good news, markets can take bad news, but markets just cannot take the uncertainty.
99 percent of traders lose money, so going with the mass is not a good idea.

summary: Historical framing of gold: price fixed by UK for a century, market data from 1973; three spikes - 1980 Iran revolution/oil crisis, 2008 Lehman, 2020 COVID. Logic: global crisis forces rate cuts, money exits deposits into gold.
lessons: Gold spikes when a global crisis forces central banks to slash rates - near-zero deposit rates make yieldless gold attractive.
Whether to buy gold depends on your view of how long the crisis and the low-rate regime will last.
quotes: Whenever there is a problem faced by the entire world, the gold prices will shoot up.

summary: Post-breakout consolidation 8,800-9,350; RBI announcement day saw Bank Nifty crash then surge (private bank index +7%, Axis +15%); PCR 0.88-0.9 = oversold despite 20% rally; 9,000-10,000 OI range; pent-up auto demand thesis.
lessons: Put-call ratio ~0.9 after a 20% rally means still oversold - room for short covering, not top.
The more times a level (38.2% Fib ~9,300) is tested, the higher the odds of breakout.

summary: Explains the historic negative WTI print: contracts marked for physical delivery with storage full forced holders to pay to exit, driving May-2020 futures to -$37 while June contracts stayed normal. Analogy-driven, with explicit disclaimers.
lessons: Contracts expiring into physical delivery can print absurd prices when storage is exhausted - know delivery mechanics before holding.
Negative prices were contract-specific: the next-month contract kept trading at normal positive levels.
quotes: Storage facilities are completely full, no more storage is possible, and that created a huge panic among the buyers.

summary: Franklin Templeton wound up six debt schemes (~30,000 crore) after redemption pressure; explains the butterfly effect - HNI option sellers had pledged these debt funds as collateral, exchanges zeroed collateral value, forcing liquidation that hit Friday's market.
lessons: Option sellers pledge debt funds/FDs/liquid funds as collateral instead of paying cash margin
Exchange collateral haircuts can jump to 100% overnight - pledged positions then force-liquidate
Whatever happens anywhere in the world, the stock market feels it first
quotes: Remember, whatever happens anywhere in the world, the first one to be affected will be the stock market.

summary: Two case studies where technicians were trapped: RBI's May 2018 FII window opening in HDFC Bank (cash-futures arb by funds crushed late buyers) and the 2011 flash crash from a broker's basket-order error (Nifty -15% intraday, futures only -3-4%). Conclusion: no single system works.
lessons: Look at everything - news, flows, regulation - never one indicator alone
When a known buying window opens, front-runners buy in cash and short futures; late chart-followers get trapped
Order-entry errors can crash markets 15% in minutes and reverse; stop-losses get hit both ways
If one system reliably worked, everyone would follow it and it would stop working
quotes: No particular system works in the stock market. If any one system worked, everybody would be following that.

summary: Argues index options beat stock options: indices cannot crash 50-60% in a day (DHFL -65%, Infibeam -70% did), index margins are half of stock margins for similar contract size, far-strike liquidity is deep, no physical delivery, panic exits always available.
lessons: Return on margin matters, not how much the underlying moves - index gives 6-7% on margin vs 4% for a stock moving twice as much
Stocks can gap 50-70% overnight; indices are circuit-protected
Index options keep liquidity in far strikes and later months; stock options do not
No physical delivery headache in index options
quotes: At the end of the day, what matters is the return on our investment. It is not how many percent the underlying moves.

summary: Monthly P&L review: April profit 66.3 lakh on ~95 lakh starting capital after 45 lakh in first two weeks; attributes windfall to India VIX collapse 80-85 to ~40 and Nifty clearing the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement (9300-9400) toward 9900-10000; March also +50 lakh selling calls.
lessons: High collapsing VIX plus a clear directional view is where option sellers make windfall profits - not repeatable monthly
Know when to exit: he closed nearly all positions after the Fibonacci target hit
Markets factor in known bad news (efficient market) - shorting after visible bad news is how traders get squeezed
A trader can profit in a falling market and lose in a rising one - the view matters, not the market's direction

strategies.name: Put-selling ladder in collapsing-VIX rebound
strategies.construction: Sold puts across strikes from ~6,100 to 9,000 during April 2020 recovery
strategies.numbers: April profit 66,30,478 on ~95L capital; VIX 80-85 -> 55-60 -> ~40; June 9000PE sold at 500, closed 180
strategies.best_regime: post-crash VIX collapse with market refusing to make new lows
strategies.adjustments: not detailed in this episode
strategies.risks: windfall not repeatable; VIX normalizes; requires conviction view

quotes: A trader can make profit even in a falling market and lose money even in a rising market - it is the view of the trader that is more important.
Markets are irrational and can continue to be irrational until you go bankrupt.

summary: Two-year Reliance thesis: refinery scale and superior GRMs plus the Jio pivot from commodity to telecom/retail argue for a PE re-rating from ~25 toward 40-50, implying Rs 2,500-3,000; documents the Jio stake-sale wave and the Rs 1,257 rights issue; buy on fundamentals, time on technicals, or use cash-secured puts/SIP.
lessons: Commodity businesses get PE ~10-11; telecom/retail get 40-150+ - business-mix change drives re-rating more than earnings alone.
Choose WHAT to buy from fundamentals; choose WHEN from technicals, cash-secured puts, or SIP.
A decade of flat price followed by breakout can compress years of return into two - equity payoffs are non-linear.
quotes: The biggest risk in your life is not taking any risk.

summary: Century-scale argument against crash calls: 100 years of Dow history shows every major crash (1929 ~90%, dot-com, Lehman) was followed by a powerful rebound; India's 1992/2000/2008/2020 parallels; Nifty PE ~16 sits in the historical buy zone (15-16) vs 28-30 sell zone; advises staggered ETF investing and cash-secured puts; '7500 bottom already made'.
lessons: Markets are unpredictable short-term but mean-revert upward across decades - every crash has been the entry for the next bull.
PE 15-16 has historically been an accumulation zone; 28-30 a distribution zone for Indian indices.
Contrarians win long-term; momentum target-setting is a different game - know which one you are playing.
Prefer broad ETFs over stock-picking unless you can dissect financials.

strategies.name: Staggered index investing with cash-secured puts
strategies.construction: SIP into a Nifty 50 ETF; optionally place cash-secured puts at desired lower entries
strategies.numbers: Nifty PE ~16 (May 2020); historical buy zone 15-16, sell zone 28-30; Dow 1929 crash ~90%; 1982-2000 bull ~15x
strategies.best_regime: Post-crash pessimism; long horizon
strategies.adjustments: Add on further 5-10% falls
strategies.risks: Multi-year drawdowns; requires no-liquidity-needs capital

quotes: A bull market is born out of pessimism, grows out of skepticism, matures out of optimism and dies out of euphoria.

summary: Explains donation-tax mechanics using his charity webinar: PM/CM fund donations get 100% exemption but are capped at 10% of annual profit unless a special COVID ordinance removed the cap for PM Cares; NGO donations only 50%, still 10%-capped; net effect was an extra ~Rs 1.5 lakh personal outflow - 'tax saving is a myth'.
lessons: Donation exemptions cannot shelter trading income: 100% exemption applies only within the 10%-of-profit cap (except the PM Cares ordinance window).
Donations to approved PM/CM funds: 100% deduction; most NGOs: 50% deduction - both subject to the qualifying-limit rule.

summary: Explains the 8,950PE flash spike (0.50 to ~20 in minutes) as a probable fat-finger market buy, citing the earlier NSE episode where a broker's basket-order error crashed Nifty ~15% before reversal; notes May's three weekly expiries all closed within 9,100-9,200 despite violent daily swings; then unpacks why Reliance's rights entitlement traded 30-40 above intrinsic (staggered 25/25/50 payment schedule).
lessons: Resting limit orders far from spot can get filled by flash spikes; square off immediately - such dislocations vanish in seconds and cannot be systematically captured.
A month can be violently volatile intraday yet flat close-to-close: distance-based option selling harvests the chaos.
Staggered-payment instruments (rights entitlements) can rationally trade above intrinsic because of embedded financing value.
quotes: Sometimes the market is like a beach horse: it runs around, but always returns to the same spot.

summary: Tax primer: cash-market gains taxed at 15% STCG / 10% LTCG above 1 lakh (post-2018), while F&O profits are business income taxed at slab rates with full expense deduction. Compares individual vs corporate accounts: ~42% top personal rate vs 22-25% corporate, but MAT ~18% limits corporate loss set-off.
lessons: F&O income is business income: slab rates hurt, but expense deduction (broadband, office, salaries, depreciation) and loss set-off often win.
Individual accounts can carry trading losses forward ~8 years against future profits; corporate accounts face MAT (~18%) even in profit years, limiting set-off value.
Entity choice rule of thumb: large, consistently profitable capital -> corporate (22-25% vs ~42%); small capital or loss-prone -> individual.
Cash-market capital gains allow no expense deduction - flat 15%/10% - unlike business income.
quotes: Go and make profit first, then come to me - the auditor's answer to every F&O tax question.

summary: Q&A: debunks the short-selling 'ban' (practical cap ~500 crore plus margin), warns against 2008-pattern confirmation bias with the market at record highs, explains weekly-hedge rollover mechanics, options-vs-futures collateral treatment for MTM losses, margin-shortfall penalty slabs, and tells small-capital traders to avoid F&O.
lessons: Confirmation bias: when you want a crash you will find reasons - trade the market that is, not the pattern that 'should' repeat.
Options-seller MTM losses can be adjusted against collateral until booked; futures MTM must be paid in cash daily - know which instrument your capital can carry.
Squaring only the hedge leg instantly recreates a naked position: margin shortfall penalties run 0.5%/day (<1 lakh), 1%/day (>1 lakh), 5%/day from the sixth session.
There is no holy-grail directional formula in open interest - only guidelines plus experience.

strategies.name: Monthly short option + weekly protective hedge
strategies.construction: Sell far-month option; buy near-week option slightly OTM below breakeven; re-buy weekly
strategies.numbers: 9,000PE July sold (>100 premium), 8,900PE weekly bought; margin ~50,000 vs >1,00,000 unhedged
strategies.best_regime: credit selling with black-swan protection
strategies.adjustments: roll weekly wing; broker far-strike restrictions are the friction
strategies.risks: weekly wing expires worthless after rallies; rollover cost creep

quotes: People expect a crash because they studied 2008 - the market is not obliged to repeat anyone's pattern.

summary: Post-market: overnight Dow futures -1000+ triggered bank-led selling (ICICI -5.5%); FII streak-selling 6000+ crore in four sessions; India VIX +5.69% above 30; speaker sold 1600 puts hedged with 1500 puts and Bank Nifty call ladder 21500-23000; range view 9500 support / 10350-10500 resistance.
lessons: FIIs buy in streaks and sell in streaks; the risk-on/risk-off flip, not the level, creates volatility.
VIX above 30 signals a high-volatility regime: violent intraday swings inside a stable range.
Whenever you sell an option, buy one too - margin falls and black swans are insured.

strategies.construction: Sell 1600 put, buy 1500 put (June expiry); Bank Nifty call ladder 21500/22000/22500/23000 with weekly hedges
strategies.numbers: FII context: -6000 crore in 4 sessions; VIX 30+

strategies.adjustments: Weekly hedge rolls to cut margin
strategies.risks: Range break below support

quotes: If they start buying they will keep on buying; if they start selling they will keep on selling.

summary: Builds a limited-risk call ratio on the post-COVID rally: buy 1x 10,500 Aug CE @360, sell 3x 11,000 Aug CE, buy 2x 11,500 Aug CE; net credit ~1,900; margin ~63,000 effective; max profit ~37,000 at Nifty 11,000; breakeven 11,253; max loss ~37,000 above 11,500; anchored on 200-DMA + 50% Fibonacci resistance.
lessons: Turn a 'resistance holds' view into a credit ratio spread; add far calls to cap the unlimited-risk tail.
Net-credit gating: if the structure is a debit in the near expiry, step out to the far month where it pays you.
Margin-benefit rules let 2-3 lakh accounts run defined-risk ratio structures.

strategies.name: Limited-risk call ratio spread (1:3:2)
strategies.construction: Buy 1x 10,500 CE (Aug), sell 3x 11,000 CE (Aug), buy 2x 11,500 CE (Aug)
strategies.numbers: Net credit ~Rs 1,900; margin ~Rs 65,000 (Rs 63,000 effective); max profit ~Rs 37,000 at Nifty 11,000; upper breakeven 11,253; max loss ~Rs 37,000 above 11,500
strategies.best_regime: After a sharp rally, into strong resistance (200-DMA + 50% retracement of 12,400->7,500)
strategies.adjustments: Exit all legs together; partial exit leaves naked short calls
strategies.risks: Sustained breakout above 11,500 hits max loss; requires two-month view

summary: Q&A batch: no fixed monthly returns as an option seller (HNI pattern: FD/debt-fund collateral is the primary income, trading is a bonus); margin shortfall penalty slabs; no safe strategy and no permanently strong company; minimum capital views; index fund vs futures; physical-delivery discipline; arbitrage vs reverse arbitrage on discounted futures.
lessons: Anchor option-selling expectations to collateral yield: primary income is interest on pledged debt funds; trading profit is supplementary and irregular.
Margin shortfall penalty: 0.5% of shortfall below 1 lakh, 1% above it, rising to 5% if the breach repeats beyond five sessions - never overtrade your collateral.
There is no safe strategy and no permanently fundamentally strong company - Reliance Communications/Infrastructure/Capital were once blue chips; understand risk and reward per strategy.
Squaring off stock-option positions before 3:30 pm on expiry avoids physical-delivery auction risk, especially in low-liquidity names.

strategies.name: Collateral-funded option selling (HNI pattern)
strategies.construction: Pledge debt mutual funds/bank FDs as collateral; sell options against the margin; keep interest as primary return
strategies.numbers: Stated pattern: 6-7% interest on debt funds while trading on pledged limit
strategies.best_regime: Wealthy, income-focused sellers who accept trading as a bonus stream
strategies.adjustments: Not applicable - structural allocation
strategies.risks: Trading losses eat the collateral cushion; interest is not guaranteed against credit events

strategies.name: Reverse arbitrage on futures discount
strategies.construction: Sell physical shares held in demat, buy the discounted futures; converge at expiry and reverse both
strategies.numbers: Example: stock 1000 spot vs 990 futures captures ~10 points
strategies.best_regime: Futures at significant discount (e.g., Nifty futures 80-90 points under spot)
strategies.adjustments: Hold to convergence
strategies.risks: Only works if shares already held; capital locked; convergence timing

quotes: stock market is not for the people who are expecting a regular or fixed return
there is no such thing called a safe strategy

summary: Counters technical analysts calling for a 7500 retest: after the October 2008 Lehman low (2252), Nifty doubled within a year and the low was never retested; the COVID candle's high was 11400 - once crossed, it may never be retested. COVID fell less than 50% (vs 2008's >50%), so recovery may be slower, but 15000 arrives before 7500. Investment timing: invest when you have surplus cash; exit when you need the money.
lessons: Post-crash lows of true panic candles (2008, 2020) are historically not retested once the recovery candle's high is crossed - drawdown bottoming behaves asymmetrically.
The depth of the crash sets the pace of recovery: 2008's >50% fall doubled in a year; 2020's shallower fall implies a slower but persistent recovery.
The right time to invest is when you have surplus cash; the right time to exit is when you need the money - waiting for the 'right opportunity' is itself a losing strategy.
quotes: the right time to invest is when you have surplus cash. The right time to exit is when you need the money

summary: Members-first review of three July structures: Bank Nifty short straddle started at 21500 (2400 combined premium), shifted to 22000 then 22500 as the market rallied, plus weekly reference trades (~8 lakh on ~1 crore); Nifty put ratio spread (buy 10500 PE 750 qty @430; sell double 10000/9500/9000 PEs, lower breakeven 9500) netting ~4.23 lakh including weeklies; and a naked ITM 22000 PE + 25000 CE reference on 80 lakh capital. Core claim: static backtests miss shifting strikes plus weekly overlays - no system works unadjusted.
lessons: A short straddle is a living position: when the market trends, shift the straddle to the new ATM instead of nursing the old strike - movement with the market is the edge backtests cannot capture.
Ratio spreads with a defended support (9500) win in both directions: the long put lost 1.84 lakh as the market rallied, but repeated short-put rounds returned ~4.24 lakh plus weekly overlay.
No mechanical system survives unadjusted: if one did, it would be arbitraged away - adjustment and position movement are the actual skill.
Late entrants should not chase a running trade: the risk-reward at entry is gone; wait for the next series and start fresh (genericized member guidance).

strategies.name: Shifting short straddle (Bank Nifty)
strategies.construction: Sell ATM straddle monthly (21500 @2400 combined); shift to 22000, then 22500 as market trends; run weekly ATM reference trades alongside
strategies.numbers: ~3.5 lakh straddle profit + ~1.76 lakh weekly profits ≈ 8 lakh on ~1 crore capital in ~2 weeks (July 2020)

strategies.adjustments: Shift straddle up/down on sustained moves; close weekly legs before direction flips
strategies.risks: Whipsaw periods cause repeated shifts with slippage; uncapped loss if a shift is missed

strategies.construction: Buy 10500 PE (750 qty @430); sell 2x 10000 PE, 2x 9500 PE, 1x 9000 PE; lower breakeven 9500; add a second round of the same short puts after a rally
strategies.numbers: Long put -1,84,000; short legs +2,59,000 +45,000 +1,20,000; base trade +2,41,000; with weeklies ~4,23,000
strategies.best_regime: Defended support below market; mildly bullish-to-neutral
strategies.adjustments: Re-sell the short-put ladder after premium decay; keep the long put as disaster hedge
strategies.risks: Break below support with doubled short puts = accelerated loss; margin-heavy
